1.7.A Describe the structure and function of proteins.

key_concepts:
1.7.A Describe the structure and function of proteins.
1.7.A.1 Proteins comprise linear chains of amino acids connected by the formation of covalent (peptide) bonds that form between a carboxyl group (COOH) of one amino acid and an amine group (NH2) of the next amino acid, resulting in a growing peptide chain.

1.7.A.2 Amino acids are composed of a central carbon atom with a hydrogen atom, a carboxyl group, an amine group, and a variable R group covalently bound to it. The R group of an amino acid can be categorized by three possible chemical properties: hydrophobic/nonpolar, hydrophilic/polar, or ionic. The interactions of these R groups determine the structure and function of that region of the protein.
1.7.A.3 The specific sequence of amino acids in proteins determines the primary structure of a polypeptide as well as the overall shape of the protein.

1.7.A.4 Secondary structures of proteins are made through the local folding that forms from interactions between atoms of the polypeptide backbone of the amino acid chain. Hydrogen bonding forms shapes such as alpha-helices and beta-pleated sheets.
1.7.A.5 The three-dimensional shape of the tertiary structure of a protein results from the formation of hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic interactions, ionic interactions, or disulfide bridges.
1.7.A.6 The quaternary structure arises from interactions between multiple polypeptides. All four levels of a protein structure determine the function of a protein.

nodes.definition: 1.1.A Explain how the properties of water that result from its polarity and hydrogen bonding affect its biological function.
key_concepts: 1.1.A Explain how the properties of water that result from its polarity and hydrogen bonding affect its biological function.

1.1.A.1 Living systems depend on the properties of water to sustain life.
i. Water has polarity, because of the formation of polar covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen within water molecules. This polarity contributes to hydrogen bonding between and within biological molecules.
ii. Water has a high specific heat capacity, which allows for the maintenance of homeostatic body temperature within living organisms.
iii. Water has a high heat of vaporization, which allows for the evaporative cooling of the surrounding environment. In living organisms, this property allows for body temperature to be maintained.
1.1.A.2 The hydrogen bonds between adjacent polar water molecules result in cohesion, adhesion, and surface tension.

1.3.A.1
Hydrolysis is a chemical reaction involving the cleaving of covalent bonds. This type of reaction breaks down molecules into smaller molecules. When water is added to the bond between monomers in a polymer, the bond is broken. The hydrogen ion from a water molecule is added to one monomer and the hydroxyl group of the water molecule is added to the other monomer, completing the reaction.

1.3.A.2
Dehydration synthesis occurs when two smaller molecules are joined together through covalent bonding. A hydrogen ion is removed from one monomer and a hydroxyl group is removed from the other. This causes the loss of the equivalent of a water molecule from the reactants and the connection of the two remaining monomers. The connection of many monomers is known as polymerization.

nodes.name: 转录与翻译
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition:
The cell cycle is a highly regulated series of events that controls the growth and reproduction of eukaryotic cells.
i. The cell cycle consists of sequential stages of interphase (G1, S, G2), mitosis, and cytokinesis.
ii. G1 phase: The cell is metabolically active, duplicating organelles and cytosolic components.
iii. S phase: DNA is in the form of chromatin and replicates to form two sister chromatids connected at a centromere.
iv. G2 phase: Protein synthesis occurs, ATP is produced in large quantities, and centrosomes replicate.
key_concepts:
The cell cycle is a highly regulated series of events that controls the growth and reproduction of eukaryotic cells.
i. The cell cycle consists of sequential stages of interphase (G1, S, G2), mitosis, and cytokinesis.
ii. G1 phase: The cell is metabolically active, duplicating organelles and cytosolic components.
iii. S phase: DNA is in the form of chromatin and replicates to form two sister chromatids connected at a centromere.
iv. G2 phase: Protein synthesis occurs, ATP is produced in large quantities, and centrosomes replicate.

Mitosis is a process that ensures the transfer of a complete genome from a parent cell to two genetically identical daughter cells in eukaryotes.
i. Mitosis plays a role in growth, tissue repair, and asexual reproduction.
ii. Mitosis occurs in sequential steps (prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase) and alternates with interphase in the cell cycle.
iii. Prophase: Sister chromatids condense, mitotic spindle begins to form, and centrosomes move to opposite poles of the cell.
iv. Metaphase: Spindle fibers align chromosomes along the equator of the cell.
v. Anaphase: Paired sister chromatids separate as spindle fibers pull chromatids toward poles.
vi. Telophase: Mitotic spindle breaks down, a new nuclear envelope develops, and then the cytoplasm divides.
vii. Cytokinesis: A cleavage furrow forms in animal cells or a cell plate forms in plant cells, resulting in two new daughter cells.
A number of internal controls or checkpoints regulate progression through the cell cycle.
Interactions between cyclins and cyclin-dependent kinases control the cell cycle.

key_concepts:
BIG IDEA 1: EVOLUTION
The process of evolution drives the diversity and unity of life. Evolution is a change in the genetic makeup of a population over time, with natural selection as its major driving mechanism. Darwin’s theory, which is supported by evidence from many scientific disciplines, states that inheritable variations occur in individuals in a population. Due to competition for limited resources, individuals with more favorable genetic variations are more likely to survive and produce more offspring, thus passing traits to future generations.

7.2 Natural Selection
Explain how natural selection affects populations.
7.2.A.1
Natural selection is a major mechanism of evolution. Natural selection acts on phenotypic variations in populations.
7.2.A.2
Evolution is also driven by random occurrences. Mutations are random and are not directed by environmental or organismal needs. Some mutations are beneficial, increasing the fitness of the organism, while others are harmful, decreasing the fitness of the organism. Mutations are the primary source of new genetic variation in a population.

7.2.A.3
Environments change and apply selective pressures to populations. Evolution occurs when the frequency of alleles in a population changes over time due to natural selection. The unequal survival and reproduction of organisms with different phenotypes, caused by natural selection, can lead to the evolution of populations.

7.2.B
Explain how natural selection affects individuals and populations.
7.2.B.1
Organisms with heritable traits that are better suited to their environment tend to survive and produce more offspring than organisms with less suitable traits. This differential survival and reproduction is the process of natural selection.

nodes.definition: Explain how the properties of water that result from its polarity and hydrogen bonding affect its biological function.
key_concepts: Explain how the properties of water that result from its polarity and hydrogen bonding affect its biological function.
Living systems depend on the properties of water to sustain life.

Water has polarity, because of the formation of polar covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen within water molecules. This polarity contributes to hydrogen bonding between and within biological molecules.
The hydrogen bonds between adjacent polar water molecules result in cohesion, adhesion, and surface tension.

BIG IDEA 3: INFORMATION STORAGE AND TRANSMISSION: Living systems store, retrieve, transmit, and respond to information essential to life processes. Genetic information provides for continuity of life, and, in most cases, this information is passed from parent to offspring via DNA. Nonheritable information transmission influences behavior within and between cells, organisms, and populations. These behaviors are directed by underlying genetic information, and responses to information are vital to natural selection and evolution. Genetic information is a repository of instructions necessary for the survival, growth, and reproduction of the organism. Genetic variation can be advantageous for the long-term survival and evolution of a species.

UNIT 6: Gene Expression and Regulation: Developing Understanding: Progressing from the continuity of life to gene expression, students gain in-depth knowledge about nucleic acids and their role in gene expression in this unit. There is also a finer focus on the comparison between the structures of DNA and RNA. This unit highlights how an individual’s genotype is physically expressed through their phenotype, thus emphasizing the importance of protein synthesis (transcription and translation) in gene expression. Regulation of gene expression and cell specialization are instrumental in ensuring survival within an individual and across populations.

FUN-3.C.1 The chain rule provides a way to differentiate composite functions.

UNIT 3 Developing Understanding
In this unit, students learn how to differentiate composite functions using the chain rule and apply that understanding to determine derivatives of implicit and inverse functions. Students need to understand that for composite functions, y is a function of u while u is a function of x. Leibniz notation for the chain rule, dy/dx = dy/du * du/dx, accounts for these relationships.

UNIT 3 Preparing for the AP Exam
Mastery of the chain rule and its applications is essential for success on the AP Exam. The chain rule will be the target of assessment for many questions and a necessary step along the way for others. One common error is not recognizing when the chain rule applies, especially in composite functions such as sin²x, tan(2x - 1), and e^(x²).

It is critical that students grasp the relationship between integration and differentiation as expressed in the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus—a central idea in AP Calculus.

CHA-2
Derivatives allow us to determine rates of change at an instant by applying limits to knowledge about rates of change over intervals.

CHA-3
Derivatives allow us to solve real-world problems involving rates of change.

CHA-4
Definite integrals allow us to solve problems involving the accumulation of change over an interval.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.definition:
1.5.A  Represent the ground-state electron configuration of an atom of an element or its ions using the Aufbau principle.

ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE
1.5.A.1  The atom is composed of negatively charged electrons and a positively charged nucleus that is made of protons and neutrons.
1.5.A.3  In atoms and ions, the electrons can be thought of as being in “shells (energy levels)” and “subshells (sublevels),” as described by the ground-state electron configuration. Inner electrons are called core electrons, and outer electrons are called valence electrons. The electron configuration is explained by quantum mechanics, as delineated in the Aufbau principle and exemplified in the periodic table of the elements.
key_concepts:
1.5.A  Represent the ground-state electron configuration of an atom of an element or its ions using the Aufbau principle.

ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE
1.5.A.1  The atom is composed of negatively charged electrons and a positively charged nucleus that is made of protons and neutrons.
1.5.A.3  In atoms and ions, the electrons can be thought of as being in “shells (energy levels)” and “subshells (sublevels),” as described by the ground-state electron configuration. Inner electrons are called core electrons, and outer electrons are called valence electrons. The electron configuration is explained by quantum mechanics, as delineated in the Aufbau principle and exemplified in the periodic table of the elements.

1.6.A  Explain the relationship between the photoelectron spectrum of an atom or ion and: i. The ground-state electron configuration of the species. ii. The interactions between the electrons and the nucleus.

ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE
1.6.A.1  The energies of the electrons in a given shell can be measured experimentally with photoelectron spectroscopy (PES). The position of each peak in the PES spectrum is related to the energy required to remove an electron from the corresponding subshell, and the relative height of each peak is (ideally) proportional to the number of electrons in that subshell.

1.7.A  Explain the relationship between trends in atomic properties of elements and electronic structure and periodicity.

ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE
1.7.A.1  The organization of the periodic table is based on patterns of recurring properties of the elements, which are explained by patterns of ground-state electron configurations and the presence of completely or partially filled shells (and subshells) of electrons in atoms.
1.7.A.2  Trends in atomic properties within the periodic table (periodicity) can be predicted by the position of the element on the periodic table and qualitatively understood using Coulomb’s law, the shell model, and the concepts of shielding and effective nuclear charge. These properties include: i. Ionization energy ii. Atomic and ionic radii iii. Electron affinity iv. Electronegativity.

1.5.A.2 Coulomb’s law is used to calculate the force between two charged particles.

1.5.A.3 In atoms and ions, the electrons can be thought of as being in “shells (energy levels)” and “subshells (sublevels),” as described by the ground-state electron configuration. Inner electrons are called core electrons, and outer electrons are called valence electrons. 1.5.A.4 The relative energy required to remove an electron from different subshells of an atom or ion or from the same subshell in different atoms or ions (ionization energy) can be estimated through a qualitative application of Coulomb’s law. This energy is related to the distance from the nucleus and the effective (shield) charge of the nucleus.

key_concepts:
1.3.C.2
The arithmetic operators consist of addition +, subtraction -, multiplication *, division /, and remainder %. An arithmetic operation that uses two int values will evaluate to an int value. An arithmetic operation that uses at least one double value will evaluate to a double value.

1.3.C.5
Operators can be used to construct compound expressions. At compile time, numeric values are associated with operators according to operator precedence to determine how they are grouped. Parentheses can be used to modify operator precedence. Multiplication, division, and remainder have precedence over addition and subtraction. Operators with the same precedence are evaluated from left to right.

1.3.C.3
When dividing numeric values that are both int values, the result is only the integer portion of the quotient. When dividing numeric values that use at least one double value, the result is the quotient.

1.3.C.4
The remainder operator % is used to compute the remainder when one number a is divided by another number b.

nodes.name: 修辞情境
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students evaluate, synthesize, and cite research to support their arguments.
key_concepts: Students evaluate, synthesize, and cite research to support their arguments.
Students read and analyze rhetorical elements and their effects in nonfiction texts—including images as forms of text—from a range of disciplines and historical periods.

The AP English Language and Composition course focuses on the development and revision of evidence-based analytic and argumentative writing, the rhetorical analysis of nonfiction texts, and the decisions writers make as they compose and revise.
Students will analyze what makes others’ arguments convincing or confusing, engaging or dull, persuasive or powerless.

Students evaluate, synthesize, and cite research to support their arguments. Additionally, they read and analyze rhetorical elements and their effects in nonfiction texts—including images as forms of text—from a range of disciplines and historical periods.

The course guides students in becoming curious, critical, and responsive readers of diverse texts and becoming flexible, reflective writers of texts addressed to diverse audiences for diverse purposes. The reading and writing students do in the course should deepen and expand their understanding of how written language functions rhetorically: to communicate writers’ intentions and elicit readers’ responses in particular situations.
Students develop the skills of rhetorical analysis and composition as they repeatedly practice analyzing others’ arguments, then compose their own arguments.

KC-5.3.II.i
Reconstruction and the Civil War ended slavery, altered relationships between the states and the federal government, and led to debates over new definitions of citizenship, particularly regarding the rights of African Americans, women, and other minorities.
key_concepts:
KC-5.3.II.i
Reconstruction and the Civil War ended slavery, altered relationships between the states and the federal government, and led to debates over new definitions of citizenship, particularly regarding the rights of African Americans, women, and other minorities.

KC-5.3.II.A
The 13th Amendment abolished slavery, while the 14th and 15th amendments granted African Americans citizenship, equal protection under the laws, and voting rights.

KC-5.3.II.C
Efforts by radical and moderate Republicans to change the balance of power between Congress and the presidency and to reorder race relations in the defeated South yielded some short-term successes. Reconstruction opened up political opportunities and other leadership roles to former slaves, but it ultimately failed, due both to determined Southern resistance and the North’s waning resolve.

KC-5.3.II.E
Segregation, violence, Supreme Court decisions, and local political tactics progressively stripped away African American rights, but the 14th and 15th amendments eventually became the basis for court decisions upholding civil rights in the 20th century.

key_concepts: Explain the causes and effects of the innovations in technology, agriculture, and commerce over time.
Innovations including textile machinery, steam engines, interchangeable parts, the telegraph, and agricultural inventions increased the efficiency of production methods.
Legislation and judicial systems supported the development of roads, canals, and railroads, which extended and enlarged markets and helped foster regional interdependence.

Entrepreneurs helped to create a market revolution in production and commerce, in which market relationships between producers and consumers came to prevail as the manufacture of goods became more organized.

nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Explain the causes and effects of the innovations in technology, agriculture, and commerce over time.
key_concepts: Explain the causes and effects of the innovations in technology, agriculture, and commerce over time.
Innovations including textile machinery, steam engines, interchangeable parts, the telegraph, and agricultural inventions increased the efficiency of production methods.
Legislation and judicial systems supported the development of roads, canals, and railroads, which extended and enlarged markets and helped foster regional interdependence.
The changes caused by the market revolution had significant effects on U.S. society, workers’ lives, and gender and family relations.

nodes.name: 1945-1980 冷战
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Explain how and why various native populations in the period before European contact interacted with the natural environment in North America.
key_concepts: Explain how and why various native populations in the period before European contact interacted with the natural environment in North America.

The spread of maize cultivation from present-day Mexico northward into the present-day American Southwest and beyond supported economic development, settlement, advanced irrigation, and social diversification among societies.
Societies responded to the aridity of the Great Basin and the grasslands of the western Great Plains by developing largely mobile lifestyles.

In the Northeast, the Mississippi River Valley, and along the Atlantic seaboard, some societies developed mixed agricultural and hunter-gatherer economies that favored the development of permanent villages.
Societies in the Northwest and present-day California supported themselves by hunting and gathering, and in some areas developed settled communities supported by the vast resources of the ocean.

Legislation and judicial systems supported the development of roads, canals, and railroads, which extended and enlarged markets and helped foster regional interdependence. Transportation networks linked the North and Midwest more closely than they linked regions in the South.

Entrepreneurs helped to create a market revolution in production and commerce, in which market relationships between producers and consumers came to prevail as the manufacture of goods became more organized.

nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition:
KC-5.3.II.i
Reconstruction and the Civil War ended slavery, altered relationships between the states and the federal government, and led to debates over new definitions of citizenship, particularly regarding the rights of African Americans, women, and other minorities.
key_concepts:
KC-5.3.II.i
Reconstruction and the Civil War ended slavery, altered relationships between the states and the federal government, and led to debates over new definitions of citizenship, particularly regarding the rights of African Americans, women, and other minorities.

KC-5.3.II.A
The 13th Amendment abolished slavery, while the 14th and 15th amendments granted African Americans citizenship, equal protection under the laws, and voting rights.

KC-5.3.II.C
Efforts by radical and moderate Republicans to change the balance of power between Congress and the presidency and to reorder race relations in the defeated South yielded some short-term successes. Reconstruction opened up political opportunities and other leadership roles to former slaves, but it ultimately failed, due both to determined Southern resistance and the North’s waning resolve.

KC-5.3.II.D
Southern plantation owners continued to own the majority of the region’s land even after Reconstruction. Former slaves sought land ownership but generally fell short of self-sufficiency, as an exploitative and soil-intensive sharecropping system limited blacks’ and poor whites’ access to land in the South.

nodes.definition: Explain the causes and effects of westward expansion from 1844 to 1877.
key_concepts: Explain the causes and effects of westward expansion from 1844 to 1877.
The desire for access to natural and mineral resources and the hope of many settlers for economic opportunities or religious refuge led to an increased migration to and settlement in the West.
Advocates of annexing western lands argued that Manifest Destiny and the superiority of American institutions compelled the United States to expand its borders westward to the Pacific Ocean.
Westward migration was boosted during and after the Civil War by the passage of new legislation promoting western transportation and economic development.

nodes.name: 贫困与不平等
nodes.subject: humanities
nodes.definition: Learners will develop skills of independent enquiry and learn about appropriate research methods and methodology.
key_concepts: Learners will develop skills of independent enquiry and learn about appropriate research methods and methodology.
Candidates undertake independent research on a topic of their own choice. They devise and develop a research question and then conduct personal research to answer that question.

Candidates should select research methods that are appropriate for their chosen topic. The research can be based on primary and/or secondary evidence, depending on the subject matter and the approach. The types of research methods that might be used are:
• reviewing the secondary literature in the field
• close analysis of texts
• producing evidence through other qualitative research methods (e.g. ethnography, interviews, focus groups)
• analysis and evaluation of statistical or other numerical data
• producing evidence through other quantitative research methods (e.g. surveys, experiments)
• a mixture of the methods above.

The study of the reasons why particular sets of methods are appropriate for specific academic subject areas is known as research methodology. Candidates are expected to engage with the methodology underlying their choice of research methods, and consider the impact of their choice on their report.

key_concepts: The aims are to enable students to: • acknowledge and understand the diversity of perspectives on global issues • develop the ability to evaluate claims and evidence • make independent judgements supported by reasoning and evidence, and understand the importance of justifying their own opinions • become effective researchers, using appropriate sources to support judgements and understanding of research processes • develop their ability to reflect on their own learning and judgements and on their work with others • develop a range of effective written and spoken communication skills.

Cambridge International AS & A Level Global Perspectives & Research develops learners’ thinking skills of analysis, evaluation and synthesis through considering a range of global topics. Learners will develop skills of independent enquiry and learn about appropriate research methods and methodology.

The Critical Path offers a systematic approach to teaching and learning where learners develop the ability to deconstruct and reconstruct arguments about global issues through personal research and interrogation of evidence. By reflecting on the implications of their research and the personal judgements it leads them to make, students learn to communicate their findings and ideas through a range of appropriate formats.

The Critical Path is an approach to teaching and learning that provides a systematic way for learners to develop the skills of research, reasoning and communication. These valuable thinking and reasoning skills are useful for a range of subjects and can also be used in higher education and a wide range of careers.

nodes.name: 资产阶级革命与资本主义制度确立

nodes.definition: 了解英国资产阶级革命、美国独立战争和法国大革命的历史背景与过程，理解资产阶级革命的共同特征与差异。
key_concepts: 了解英国资产阶级革命、美国独立战争和法国大革命的历史背景与过程，理解资产阶级革命的共同特征与差异。
认识资本主义制度确立的历史意义，理解君主立宪制与民主共和制的基本特征。
了解资本主义制度在世界范围内的扩展，认识其对人类社会发展的深远影响。

nodes.name: 工业革命
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: 本课程以通史的叙事框架，展示中国历史和世界历史发展的基本过程。本课程共有24个专题，是高中历史学习的基本内容。
key_concepts: 本课程以通史的叙事框架，展示中国历史和世界历史发展的基本过程。本课程共有24个专题，是高中历史学习的基本内容。
通过对中外重大历史事件、历史人物和历史现象的叙述，展现人类发展进程中丰富的历史文化遗产，以及人类社会从古至今、从分散到整体、社会形态从低级到高级的发展历程。

nodes.name: 马克思主义与俄国革命
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: 马克思主义根据人类社会生产力与生产关系基本矛盾的不同性质，把人类历史发展分为原始社会、奴隶社会、封建社会、资本主义社会和共产主义社会几种社会形态。
key_concepts: 马克思主义根据人类社会生产力与生产关系基本矛盾的不同性质，把人类历史发展分为原始社会、奴隶社会、封建社会、资本主义社会和共产主义社会几种社会形态。
认识五四爱国运动的历史意义，认识马克思主义在中国的传播与中国共产党成立对中国革命的深远影响。

nodes.name: 世界殖民体系与亚非拉民族独立运动
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: 了解西方列强对亚非拉地区的殖民扩张，认识世界殖民体系的形成过程及其对殖民地半殖民地社会的影响。
key_concepts: 了解西方列强对亚非拉地区的殖民扩张，认识世界殖民体系的形成过程及其对殖民地半殖民地社会的影响。
了解拉丁美洲独立运动、亚洲觉醒和非洲抗争的基本史实，认识亚非拉民族独立运动的历史意义。
认识殖民体系的形成与瓦解是世界历史发展的重要线索之一。

nodes.name: 两次世界大战
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: 了解第一次世界大战爆发的背景与帝国主义国家间的矛盾，理解战争对世界格局的深远影响和凡尔赛—华盛顿体系的形成。
key_concepts: 了解第一次世界大战爆发的背景与帝国主义国家间的矛盾，理解战争对世界格局的深远影响和凡尔赛—华盛顿体系的形成。
了解日本军国主义的侵华罪行；通过了解正面战场和敌后战场的抗战，认识中国战场是世界反法西斯战争的东方主战场，理解十四年抗战胜利在中华民族伟大复兴中的历史意义。
了解雅尔塔体系与战后国际秩序的重建，理解联合国成立等机制对维护战后和平的意义。

nodes.name: 冷战格局
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: 通过了解第二次世界大战后国际格局的变化，理解冷战的发生与发展，认识两极格局的特征及其对世界的影响。
key_concepts: 通过了解第二次世界大战后国际格局的变化，理解冷战的发生与发展，认识两极格局的特征及其对世界的影响。
了解杜鲁门主义、马歇尔计划、北约与华约的对峙，认识美苏争霸对国际关系的影响。
通过对古巴导弹危机、越南战争、阿富汗战争等热点事件的了解，理解冷战中的局部冲突与世界格局的复杂性。

nodes.name: 全球化与多极化
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: 了解世界历史发展的多样性，理解和尊重世界各国、各民族的文化传统，具有广阔的国际视野，树立正确的文化观。
key_concepts: 了解世界历史发展的多样性，理解和尊重世界各国、各民族的文化传统，具有广阔的国际视野，树立正确的文化观。
通过中外历史上重要的事件、人物和现象，展现人类社会从古至今、从分散到整体、从低级到高级的发展历程。
拓宽国际视野，形成开放的世界意识。

key_concepts: 历史选择性必修课程是学生根据个人兴趣、升学需求而选择修习的课程，设《国家制度与社会治理》《经济与社会生活》和《文化交流与传播》三个模块。

nodes.name: 文化史与思想史
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: 通过了解春秋战国时期的经济发展和政治变动，理解战国时期变法运动的必然性；了解老子、孔子学说；通过孟子、荀子、庄子等了解“百家争鸣”的局面及其意义。

nodes.definition: 细胞是生物体结构和功能的基本单位。细胞的分裂、分化和生长是细胞重要的生命活动。
key_concepts: 细胞是生物体结构和功能的基本单位。细胞的分裂、分化和生长是细胞重要的生命活动。
识别动植物细胞的结构并说出其异同点，说明细胞是生物体结构和功能的基本单位。
为学生提供多种生物材料，指导学生制作临时装片，利用显微镜进行观察，使学生初步学会使用显微镜观察的方法，形成对细胞结构的感性认识。

nodes.name: 显微镜的使用
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 正确、规范地制作临时装片，使用显微镜进行观察，能够针对观察结果中可能出现的成像不佳等情况，从材料制备、仪器设备、操作程序等方面初步分析原因。

nodes.name: 细胞基础

nodes.name: 细胞的结构
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 动物细胞、植物细胞都具有细胞膜、细胞质、细胞核等结构。植物细胞具有不同于动物细胞的结构，如叶绿体和细胞壁。
key_concepts: 动物细胞、植物细胞都具有细胞膜、细胞质、细胞核等结构。植物细胞具有不同于动物细胞的结构，如叶绿体和细胞壁。
识别动植物细胞的结构并说出其异同点，说明细胞是生物体结构和功能的基本单位。
制作植物细胞、动物细胞的临时装片，用显微镜观察细胞结构；尝试制作植物细胞或动物细胞的结构模型。

nodes.name: 细胞的生命活动
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 细胞不同结构的功能各不相同，共同完成细胞的各项生命活动。
key_concepts: 细胞不同结构的功能各不相同，共同完成细胞的各项生命活动。
运用示意图或模型等方式，展示和说明细胞各结构的功能及其相互关系。
指导学生制作临时装片，利用显微镜进行观察，使学生初步学会使用显微镜观察的方法，形成对细胞结构的感性认识。

nodes.name: 细胞分裂
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 细胞能通过分裂和分化形成不同的组织
key_concepts: 细胞能通过分裂和分化形成不同的组织

引导学生通过观察某种器官不同组织的特点，基于事实进行科学推理，深入理解细胞分化的概念

nodes.name: 细胞分化
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 细胞能通过分裂和分化形成不同的组织
key_concepts: 细胞能通过分裂和分化形成不同的组织

nodes.name: 组织与器官
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 功能不同的组织可以形成器官，共同完成某种生理功能的器官可以形成系统。
key_concepts: 功能不同的组织可以形成器官，共同完成某种生理功能的器官可以形成系统。
绿色开花植物体的结构层次包括细胞、组织、器官和个体，高等动物体的结构层次包括细胞、组织、器官、系统和个体。
识别给定生物材料所属的结构层次，并阐明生物体在结构和功能上是一个有机整体。

nodes.name: 生物圈
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 生态系统中的生物与非生物环境相互作用，实现了物质循环和能量流动。
key_concepts: 生态系统中的生物与非生物环境相互作用，实现了物质循环和能量流动。
从结构与功能的角度，阐明生态系统中的生产者、消费者、分解者以及非生物环境是一个有机整体。
分析人类活动对生态环境造成破坏的实例，形成保护生物圈的社会责任意识。
结合具体实例，引导学生分析生态系统中各成分的作用及其相互关系，并用恰当的形式呈现，发展学生的建模思维。

nodes.name: 生态因素
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 生态因素能够影响生物的生活和分布，生物能够适应和影响环境
key_concepts: 生态因素能够影响生物的生活和分布，生物能够适应和影响环境
从结构与功能的角度，阐明生态系统中的生产者、消费者、分解者以及非生物环境是一个有机整体
通过资料分析、调查、实验探究等活动，引导学生认识生物与环境的关系
探究影响鼠妇（或蚯蚓等）分布的环境因素，探究植被类型与环境湿度或温度之间的关系

nodes.name: 生物圈的范围
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 生态系统是由生产者、消费者、分解者与非生物环境构成的有机整体。
key_concepts: 生态系统是由生产者、消费者、分解者与非生物环境构成的有机整体。
从结构与功能的角度，阐明生态系统中的生产者、消费者、分解者以及非生物环境是一个有机整体。

nodes.name: 食物链与食物网
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 生态系统中不同生物之间通过捕食关系形成了食物链和食物网
key_concepts: 生态系统中不同生物之间通过捕食关系形成了食物链和食物网

nodes.name: 生物圈是最大的生态系统
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 生物圈是包含多种类型生态系统的最大生态系统
key_concepts: 生物圈是包含多种类型生态系统的最大生态系统
分析人类活动对生态环境造成破坏的实例，形成保护生物圈的社会责任意识。
通过各种途径收集生物圈的相关资料，模拟召开“生物圈国际保护”研讨会，结合本地实际讨论如何保护生物圈。

nodes.name: 生态系统的组成
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 生态系统是由生产者、消费者、分解者与非生物环境构成的有机整体。
key_concepts: 生态系统是由生产者、消费者、分解者与非生物环境构成的有机整体。

nodes.name: 绿色植物整体结构
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 植物分布广泛，直接或间接地为其他生物提供食物和能量；植物参与生物圈中的水循环，维持生物圈中的碳氧平衡。
key_concepts: 植物分布广泛，直接或间接地为其他生物提供食物和能量；植物参与生物圈中的水循环，维持生物圈中的碳氧平衡。
通过本主题的学习，学生能够理解植物体的构造与功能、植物的生活与生产、植物在生物圈中的作用。
识别给定生物材料所属的结构层次，并阐明生物体在结构和功能上是一个有机整体。

nodes.name: 种子结构与萌发
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 概念4 植物有自己的生命周期，可以制造有机物，直接或间接地为其他生物提供食物，参与生物圈的水循环，并维持碳氧平衡。
key_concepts: 概念4 植物有自己的生命周期，可以制造有机物，直接或间接地为其他生物提供食物，参与生物圈的水循环，并维持碳氧平衡。
4.1.1 种子包括种皮和胚等结构，种子萌发需要完整、有活力的胚，需要充足的空气、适宜的温度、适量的水等环境条件。
描述种子萌发的过程和条件；说明植物体的结构层次；阐明植物体在结构和功能上是一个统一整体。
实验探究活动：探究种子萌发的条件；观察根尖的结构；观察芽的结构和发育。

nodes.name: 根尖结构
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 植物通过根吸收水和无机盐，满足植物生长发育的需要。
key_concepts: 植物通过根吸收水和无机盐，满足植物生长发育的需要。
根尖是根吸收水和无机盐的主要部位。
通过实验，探究植物对水和无机盐的吸收、运输和散失过程。
实验探究活动：探究植物对水和无机盐的吸收、运输和散失。

nodes.name: 茎的运输作用
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 概念4 植物通过吸收作用和蒸腾作用参与生物圈的水循环，通过光合作用和呼吸作用参与生物圈的碳氧平衡
key_concepts: 概念4 植物通过吸收作用和蒸腾作用参与生物圈的水循环，通过光合作用和呼吸作用参与生物圈的碳氧平衡
4.2 植物通过吸收、运输和蒸腾作用参与生物圈的水循环
4.2.2 植物茎中具有运输功能的输导组织

nodes.name: 叶片结构
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 植物细胞具有不同于动物细胞的结构，如叶绿体和细胞壁等。
key_concepts: 植物细胞具有不同于动物细胞的结构，如叶绿体和细胞壁等。
识别动植物细胞的结构并说出其异同点，说明细胞是生物体结构和功能的基本单位。
指导学生在感性认识的基础上，通过比较、归纳等方法，找出不同类型细胞的共同特征，并运用模式图或模型等方式展现细胞的结构。

nodes.name: 光合作用
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 概念 3.1.5 生态系统中的物质和能量通过食物链在生物之间传递
key_concepts: 概念 3.1.5 生态系统中的物质和能量通过食物链在生物之间传递
通过本主题的学习，学生能够认识到植物分布广泛，直接或间接地为其他生物提供食物和能量；植物参与生物圈中的水循环，维持生物圈中的碳氧平衡。

nodes.name: 呼吸作用
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 概念4 植物通过光合作用和呼吸作用参与生物圈中的物质循环和能量流动，维持生物圈中的碳氧平衡。
key_concepts: 概念4 植物通过光合作用和呼吸作用参与生物圈中的物质循环和能量流动，维持生物圈中的碳氧平衡。
4.2.2 植物通过呼吸作用分解有机物，释放能量，供给植物生命活动的需要。
（2）通过实验探究绿色植物的光合作用和呼吸作用，阐明绿色植物在生物圈中的作用。

nodes.name: 蒸腾作用
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 植物通过根吸收水分，通过导管运输水分，通过叶片散失水分，从而参与生物圈中的水循环。
key_concepts: 植物通过根吸收水分，通过导管运输水分，通过叶片散失水分，从而参与生物圈中的水循环。
阐明植物在生物圈水循环中的作用。
通过实验，探究蒸腾作用的主要器官。

nodes.name: 花的结构与传粉
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 概念4 植物有自己的生命周期，可以制造有机物，直接或间接地为其他生物提供食物，参与生物圈的水循环，并维持碳氧平衡。
key_concepts: 概念4 植物有自己的生命周期，可以制造有机物，直接或间接地为其他生物提供食物，参与生物圈的水循环，并维持碳氧平衡。
4.2.1 花是植物的生殖器官，其结构有利于完成传粉和受精。
4.2.2 植物可以通过不同的媒介（如风、昆虫）完成传粉。

nodes.name: 果实与种子的形成
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 概念4 植物有自己的生命周期，可以制造有机物，直接或间接地为其他生物提供食物，参与生物圈的水循环，并维持碳氧平衡。
key_concepts: 概念4 植物有自己的生命周期，可以制造有机物，直接或间接地为其他生物提供食物，参与生物圈的水循环，并维持碳氧平衡。
4.2.2 花经过传粉和受精后形成果实和种子。
描述花的基本结构，阐明花与果实和种子形成的关系。

nodes.name: 植物的无性生殖
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 无性生殖是植物繁殖的一种方式，如扦插、嫁接等，能够保持母本的优良性状。
key_concepts: 无性生殖是植物繁殖的一种方式，如扦插、嫁接等，能够保持母本的优良性状。
通过观察或实验，描述植物的无性生殖过程，并举例说明其在农业生产中的应用。
组织学生开展植物扦插、嫁接等实践活动，体验无性生殖的技术方法。

nodes.name: 植物的主要类群
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 根据生物的形态结构、生理功能以及繁殖方式等，可以将生物分为不同的类群。
key_concepts: 根据生物的形态结构、生理功能以及繁殖方式等，可以将生物分为不同的类群。
藻类是能够进行光合作用的结构简单的生物。苔藓、蕨类、裸子植物和被子植物都具有根、茎、叶等器官的分化，植物繁殖过程逐渐摆脱了对水环境的依赖。
通过列表等多种方式，对不同生物类群的形态结构、生活环境、繁殖方式等进行比较，帮助学生逐步形成生物具有多样性和统一性的认识。

nodes.name: 人体概述
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 人体生理与健康是课程内容七个学习主题之一，包含人体概述与消化系统等基础知识。
key_concepts: 人体生理与健康是课程内容七个学习主题之一，包含人体概述与消化系统等基础知识。
获得人体生理与健康等方面的基础知识；初步形成生物学的结构与功能观等生命观念。
关注身体内外各种因素对健康的影响，在饮食作息等方面形成健康生活的态度和行为习惯。

nodes.name: 消化系统
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 5. 1 人体通过消化系统从外界获取生命活动所需的营养物质
key_concepts: 5. 1 人体通过消化系统从外界获取生命活动所需的营养物质
5.1.1 水、无机盐、糖类、蛋白质、脂质和维生素是人体生命 活动所需的主要营养物质
5.1.2 消化系统由消化道和消化腺组成

nodes.name: 呼吸系统
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 人体生理与健康主题包含呼吸系统与气体交换等内容，学生应掌握人体各系统的结构和功能。
key_concepts: 人体生理与健康主题包含呼吸系统与气体交换等内容，学生应掌握人体各系统的结构和功能。
学生能够说明呼吸系统与气体交换的基本过程，理解其对人体的重要性。
通过实验探究活动，如模拟呼吸运动或测量肺活量，帮助学生理解呼吸系统的结构与功能。

nodes.name: 循环系统
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 人体生理与健康主题包含血液循环系统相关内容，学生应掌握人体生理与健康的基础知识。
key_concepts: 人体生理与健康主题包含血液循环系统相关内容，学生应掌握人体生理与健康的基础知识。
学生应能说明血液循环系统等器官系统在维持人体正常生理功能中的作用。
通过观察模型、示意图或视频等，引导学生理解血液循环系统的结构与功能。

nodes.name: 循环与呼吸综合
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 人体生理与健康学习主题包括循环系统与呼吸系统等内容，要求学生掌握人体生理与健康的基础知识。
key_concepts: 人体生理与健康学习主题包括循环系统与呼吸系统等内容，要求学生掌握人体生理与健康的基础知识。
学生应获得人体生理与健康等方面的基础知识，初步形成结构与功能观等生命观念。
树立健康意识和社会责任感，关注身体内外各种因素对健康的影响，形成健康生活的态度和行为习惯。

nodes.name: 排泄系统
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition: 概念5 人体通过泌尿系统排出代谢废物，维持内环境的稳定
key_concepts: 概念5 人体通过泌尿系统排出代谢废物，维持内环境的稳定

nodes.definition: 阅读表现人与自然的优秀文学作品，包括古诗文名篇，体会作者通过语言和形象构建的艺术世界，借鉴其中的写作手法。
key_concepts: 阅读表现人与自然的优秀文学作品，包括古诗文名篇，体会作者通过语言和形象构建的艺术世界，借鉴其中的写作手法。
阅读表现人与社会、人与他人的古今优秀诗歌、散文、小说、戏剧等文学作品，学习欣赏、品味作品的语言、形象等，交流审美体验。
感受语言文字的美，感悟作品的思想内涵和艺术价值，能结合自己的经验，理解、欣赏和初步评价语言文字作品。

nodes.name: 古诗词比较阅读
nodes.subject: chinese
nodes.definition: 阅读表现人与社会、人与他人的古今优秀诗歌、散文、小说、戏剧等文学作品，学习欣赏、品味作品的语言、形象等，交流审美体验。
key_concepts: 阅读表现人与社会、人与他人的古今优秀诗歌、散文、小说、戏剧等文学作品，学习欣赏、品味作品的语言、形象等，交流审美体验。
引导学生客观、全面、冷静地思考问题，识别文本隐含的情感、观点、立场，体会作者运用的思维方法，如比较、分析、概括、推理等。
思维能力是指学生在语文学习过程中的联想想象、分析比较、归纳判断等认知表现。

nodes.name: 记叙文写作
nodes.subject: chinese
nodes.definition: 能根据需要，用书面语言具体明确、文从字顺地表达自己的见闻、体验和想法。
key_concepts: 能根据需要，用书面语言具体明确、文从字顺地表达自己的见闻、体验和想法。
观察周围世界，能不拘形式地写下自己的见闻、感受和想象，注意把自己觉得新奇有趣或印象最深、最受感动的内容写清楚。
关注有新鲜感的词句，并有意识地在口头和书面表达中运用。

nodes.name: 议论文写作
nodes.subject: chinese
nodes.definition: 引导学生客观、全面、冷静地思考问题，识别文本隐含的情感、观点、立场，体会作者运用的思维方法，如比较、分析、概括、推理等。

乐于探索，勤于思考，初步掌握比较、分析、概括、推理等思维方法，辩证地思考问题，有理有据、负责任地表达自己的观点。

nodes.name: 综合性作文

表达要观点鲜明、证据充分、合乎逻辑。

nodes.name: 整本书阅读方法
nodes.subject: chinese
nodes.definition: 独立阅读古今中外诗歌集、中长篇小说、散文集等文学名著，根据阅读进度完成读书笔记，针对作品的语言、形象、主题等方面的话题展开研讨。

引导学生了解阅读的多种策略，运用浏览、略读、精读等不同阅读方法；通读整本书，了解主要内容，关注整体与局部、局部与局部之间的关系。

nodes.name: 国际音标（IPA）
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: 音标是初中阶段需要学习的语音知识内容。要帮助学生学习和掌握音标，借助音标准确读出和记忆单词，为学生开展自主学习奠定基础。
key_concepts: 音标是初中阶段需要学习的语音知识内容。要帮助学生学习和掌握音标，借助音标准确读出和记忆单词，为学生开展自主学习奠定基础。
就语音知识而言，要让学生学会根据重音、意群、语调与节奏等语音方面的变化，感知说话人表达的不同意义...并进行模仿、练习和内化，学会运用语音知识更好地表达自己的意图和态度。

nodes.name: 课标核心词汇（1600词）
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: 就词汇知识而言，要让学生认识到词汇学习不是单纯的词汇记忆和机械的操练，而是要学会运用词语在特定情境中理解和表达意义。
key_concepts: 就词汇知识而言，要让学生认识到词汇学习不是单纯的词汇记忆和机械的操练，而是要学会运用词语在特定情境中理解和表达意义。
尽量以词块的形式呈现生词，引导学生关注词语的搭配和固定的表达方式，并在围绕主题意义建构结构化知识的过程中，提炼词语的搭配和固定表达方式，构建词汇语义网，积累词块，扩大词汇量。
指导学生借助构词法知识和词典、词表等工具学习词语，大胆使用新的词块自主表达意义、解决新问题。

nodes.name: 阅读策略（略读/扫读/精读）
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: 引导学生充分利用语篇知识有效获取和传递信息，表达观点和态度。

能运用一定的阅读策略，借助表格、思维导图等工具梳理书面语篇的主要信息，理解大意。
在阅读稍长的语篇材料时，能理解主要内容，推断隐含信息，表达个人看法，提出合理疑问，分析和解决问题。

nodes.name: 语篇类型识别（记叙/说明/议论）
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: 就语篇知识而言，要为学生提供接触和体验各种语篇类型的机会，指导学生学习不同文体特有的语篇结构和语言特征。
key_concepts: 就语篇知识而言，要为学生提供接触和体验各种语篇类型的机会，指导学生学习不同文体特有的语篇结构和语言特征。
引导学生围绕主题使用思维导图梳理词汇。指导学生借助构词法知识和词典、词表等工具学习词语。
在阅读稍长的语篇材料时，能理解主要内容，推断隐含信息，表达个人看法，提出合理疑问，分析和解决问题。

nodes.name: 完形填空
nodes.subject: english

nodes.name: 基础写作（短文/书信/邮件）
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: 进行书面表达时，能正确使用所学语言，格式较为规范。能参照范例，仿写简短的文段（如回复信函等），语言准确，表意得体。
key_concepts: 进行书面表达时，能正确使用所学语言，格式较为规范。能参照范例，仿写简短的文段（如回复信函等），语言准确，表意得体。
能选用正确的词语、句式和时态，通过口语或书面语篇描述、介绍人和事物，表达个人看法，表意清晰，话语基本通顺。
能结合图片、文字等提示信息，对语篇进行补充、续编或改编，语言基本准确。

nodes.name: 基础听力（对话/短文）
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: 能听懂相关主题的语篇，借助关键词句、图片等复述语篇内容。能利用语篇所给提示预测内容的发展，判断说话者的身份和关系，推断说话者的情感、态度和观点。
key_concepts: 能听懂相关主题的语篇，借助关键词句、图片等复述语篇内容。能利用语篇所给提示预测内容的发展，判断说话者的身份和关系，推断说话者的情感、态度和观点。
要让学生学会根据重音、意群、语调与节奏等语音方面的变化，感知说话人表达的不同意义，准确地理解说话人的意图和态度。
引导学生充分利用语篇知识有效获取和传递信息，表达观点和态度。

能够观察、描述地球上人口、城乡、文化等人文环境要素的基本状况，以及人类活动对自然环境的影响。

nodes.name: 世界地理分区

nodes.definition: 运用地图和相关资料，描述某地区的地理位置，简要归纳自然地理特征，说明该特征对当地人们生产生活的影响。
key_concepts: 运用地图和相关资料，描述某地区的地理位置，简要归纳自然地理特征，说明该特征对当地人们生产生活的影响。
以某地区的一种自然资源为例，说出该资源在当地的分布状况、对外输出地区以及对当地乃至世界的重要意义。
结合实例，说明某地区发展旅游业的优势。

nodes.name: 世界主要国家（日/俄/美/澳/巴西等）
nodes.subject: geography

key_concepts: 运用地图和相关资料，说出某国家的地理位置、范围、领土构成和首都，选择与该国地理位置差异明显的国家，比较它们纬度位置和海陆位置的差异。

nodes.name: 变量与函数

nodes.name: 正比例函数

nodes.name: 一次函数

nodes.name: 一次函数与二元一次方程组

nodes.name: 几何图形初步

nodes.name: 相交线与平行线

nodes.definition: 理解补角、余角、对顶角的意义。理解垂线的意义，掌握基本事实：过一点有且只有一条直线垂直于另一条直线。
key_concepts: 理解补角、余角、对顶角的意义。理解垂线的意义，掌握基本事实：过一点有且只有一条直线垂直于另一条直线。
理解点到直线的距离的意义，掌握基本事实：垂线段最短。理解平行线的概念，掌握基本事实：过直线外一点有且只有一条直线平行于这条直线。
掌握平行线的性质定理：两条平行线被第三条直线所截，同位角相等。掌握平行线的判定定理：同位角相等，两直线平行。
能运用相交线、平行线的基本性质和判定解决问题。

nodes.name: 多边形与四边形

nodes.name: A1 水的性质与生命
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition:
C1.1.1—Enzymes as catalysts
Students should understand the benefit of increasing rates of reaction in cells.
key_concepts:
C1.1.1—Enzymes as catalysts
Students should understand the benefit of increasing rates of reaction in cells.

C1.1.2—Role of enzymes in metabolism
Students should understand that metabolism is the complex network of interdependent and interacting chemical reactions occurring in living organisms. Because of enzyme specificity, many different enzymes are required by living organisms, and control over metabolism can be exerted through these enzymes.

C1.1.4—Enzymes as globular proteins with an active site for catalysis
Include that the active site is composed of a few amino acids only, but interactions between amino acids within the overall three-dimensional structure of the enzyme ensure that the active site has the necessary properties for catalysis.

C1.1.5—Interactions between substrate and active site to allow induced-fit binding
Students should recognize that both substrate and enzymes change shape when binding occurs.

nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition:
A1.1.1—Water as the medium for life
Students should appreciate that the first cells originated in water and that water remains the medium in which most processes of life occur.
key_concepts:
A1.1.1—Water as the medium for life
Students should appreciate that the first cells originated in water and that water remains the medium in which most processes of life occur.

A1.1.5—Solvent properties of water linked to its role as a medium for metabolism and for transport in plants and animals
Emphasize that a wide variety of hydrophilic molecules dissolve in water and that most enzymes catalyse reactions in aqueous solution. Students should also understand that the functions of some molecules in cells depend on them being hydrophobic and insoluble.

A1.1.2—Hydrogen bonds as a consequence of the polar covalent bonds within water molecules
Students should understand that polarity of covalent bonding within water molecules is due to unequal sharing of electrons and that hydrogen bonding due to this polarity occurs between water molecules. Students should be able to represent two or more water molecules and hydrogen bonds between them with the notation shown below to indicate polarity.

nodes.name: A2 细胞的多样性（原核/真核）
nodes.subject: biology
nodes.definition:
A1.2.6—DNA as a double helix made of two antiparallel strands of nucleotides with two strands linked by hydrogen bonding between complementary base pairs
In diagrams of DNA structure, students should draw the two strands antiparallel, but are not required to draw the helical shape. Students should show adenine (A) paired with thymine (T), and guanine (G) paired with cytosine (C). Students are not required to memorize the relative lengths of the purine and pyrimidine bases, or the numbers of hydrogen bonds.
key_concepts:
A1.2.6—DNA as a double helix made of two antiparallel strands of nucleotides with two strands linked by hydrogen bonding between complementary base pairs
In diagrams of DNA structure, students should draw the two strands antiparallel, but are not required to draw the helical shape. Students should show adenine (A) paired with thymine (T), and guanine (G) paired with cytosine (C). Students are not required to memorize the relative lengths of the purine and pyrimidine bases, or the numbers of hydrogen bonds.

A1.2.8—Role of complementary base pairing in allowing genetic information to be replicated and expressed
Students should understand that complementarity is based on hydrogen bonding.

A1.2.12—Purine-to-pyrimidine bonding as a component of DNA helix stability
Adenine–thymine (A–T) and cytosine–guanine (C–G) pairs have equal length, so the DNA helix has the same three-dimensional structure, regardless of the base sequence.

Phospholipids and other amphipathic lipids naturally form continuous sheet-like bilayers in water.

Students should understand that the hydrophobic hydrocarbon chains that form the core of a membrane have low permeability to large molecules and hydrophilic particles, including ions and polar molecules, so membranes function as effective barriers between aqueous solutions.

Emphasize that a wide variety of hydrophilic molecules dissolve in water and that most enzymes catalyse reactions in aqueous solution. Students should also understand that the functions of some molecules in cells depend on them being hydrophobic and insoluble.

B1.1.8—Hydrophobic properties of lipids
Lipids are substances in living organisms that dissolve in non-polar solvents but are only sparingly soluble in aqueous solvents. Lipids include fats, oils, waxes and steroids.

B1.2.10—Effect of polar and non-polar amino acids on tertiary structure of proteins
In proteins that are soluble in water, hydrophobic amino acids are clustered in the core of globular proteins. Integral proteins have regions with hydrophobic amino acids, helping them to embed in membranes.

nodes.name: 可持续性
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.definition: Students will be able to explain the concept of sustainable development and evaluate the role of market-based (e.g., carbon taxes) and government-led strategies in promoting environmental sustainability.
key_concepts: Students will be able to explain the concept of sustainable development and evaluate the role of market-based (e.g., carbon taxes) and government-led strategies in promoting environmental sustainability.
Students will be able to critically assess the potential conflict between the macroeconomic objectives of economic growth and environmental sustainability.

nodes.name: 不平等
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.definition: Students will be able to analyse the causes of income and wealth inequality within and between countries using tools such as the Lorenz curve and Gini coefficient.
key_concepts: Students will be able to analyse the causes of income and wealth inequality within and between countries using tools such as the Lorenz curve and Gini coefficient.
Students will be able to evaluate the economic and social impacts of inequality and assess the effectiveness of policies designed to reduce it.

nodes.name: 选题与学科
nodes.subject: ee
nodes.definition: Students will be able to select an appropriate Diploma Programme subject for their Extended Essay, ensuring it aligns with their academic interests and the subject's availability within the IB framework.
key_concepts: Students will be able to select an appropriate Diploma Programme subject for their Extended Essay, ensuring it aligns with their academic interests and the subject's availability within the IB framework.
Students will justify their subject choice by demonstrating a clear understanding of the subject's disciplinary conventions and its suitability for a 4000-word independent investigation.

nodes.name: 研究问题（RQ）
nodes.subject: ee
nodes.definition: Students will formulate a clear, focused, and arguable research question that is appropriate for an in-depth, 4000-word academic investigation within their chosen subject.
key_concepts: Students will formulate a clear, focused, and arguable research question that is appropriate for an in-depth, 4000-word academic investigation within their chosen subject.
Students will refine their initial research question through preliminary reading to ensure it is manageable, specific, and conducive to critical analysis and argument.

nodes.name: 研究方法
nodes.subject: ee
nodes.definition: Students will design and justify a coherent research methodology appropriate to their subject and research question, demonstrating an understanding of primary and/or secondary research methods.
key_concepts: Students will design and justify a coherent research methodology appropriate to their subject and research question, demonstrating an understanding of primary and/or secondary research methods.
Students will apply their chosen methodology systematically, explaining its application and acknowledging any limitations in their research process.

nodes.name: 文献综述
nodes.subject: ee
nodes.definition: Students will conduct a comprehensive review of relevant scholarly literature, situating their research question within the existing academic discourse of the field.
key_concepts: Students will conduct a comprehensive review of relevant scholarly literature, situating their research question within the existing academic discourse of the field.
Students will synthesize and critically evaluate the literature, identifying gaps, debates, or contexts that their own investigation will address.

nodes.name: 大纲与结构
nodes.subject: ee
nodes.definition: Students will construct a logical and coherent outline for their essay, ensuring the structure effectively supports the development of their argument and analysis.
key_concepts: Students will construct a logical and coherent outline for their essay, ensuring the structure effectively supports the development of their argument and analysis.
Students will organize their essay according to the formal conventions of academic writing in their subject area, including a clear introduction, development, and conclusion.

nodes.name: 论证与分析
nodes.subject: ee
nodes.definition: Students will develop a sustained, reasoned argument in response to their research question, supported by critical analysis of evidence.
key_concepts: Students will develop a sustained, reasoned argument in response to their research question, supported by critical analysis of evidence.
Students will demonstrate higher-order thinking skills by evaluating different perspectives, interpreting data or sources, and drawing well-substantiated conclusions.

nodes.name: 引用规范（MLA/APA）
nodes.subject: ee
nodes.definition: Students will consistently and accurately apply a recognized system of academic referencing (e.g., MLA, APA, Chicago) to acknowledge all sources used in their work.
key_concepts: Students will consistently and accurately apply a recognized system of academic referencing (e.g., MLA, APA, Chicago) to acknowledge all sources used in their work.
Students will understand and avoid academic misconduct by distinguishing between their own ideas and those of others through proper paraphrasing, quoting, and citation.

nodes.name: 格式规范
nodes.subject: ee
nodes.definition: Students will adhere to the formal presentation requirements for the Extended Essay, including title page, abstract, contents page, page numbering, and overall layout as specified in the EE guide.
key_concepts: Students will adhere to the formal presentation requirements for the Extended Essay, including title page, abstract, contents page, page numbering, and overall layout as specified in the EE guide.
Students will ensure their final submission is professionally presented and meets the technical requirements for assessment.

nodes.name: 初次反思
nodes.subject: ee
nodes.definition: Students will complete the first reflection session on the Reflections on planning and progress form (RPPF), reflecting on their initial ideas, the formulation of their research question, and their planning process.
key_concepts: Students will complete the first reflection session on the Reflections on planning and progress form (RPPF), reflecting on their initial ideas, the formulation of their research question, and their planning process.

nodes.name: 中期反思
nodes.subject: ee
nodes.definition: Students will complete the interim reflection on the RPPF, evaluating the progress of their research and writing, discussing challenges encountered, and outlining their plan for completion.
key_concepts: Students will complete the interim reflection on the RPPF, evaluating the progress of their research and writing, discussing challenges encountered, and outlining their plan for completion.

nodes.name: 终审面谈
nodes.subject: ee
nodes.definition: Following the completion of the Extended Essay, students will participate in a concluding interview (viva voce) with their supervisor to reflect on their learning journey, the research process, and the outcomes of their work.
key_concepts: Following the completion of the Extended Essay, students will participate in a concluding interview (viva voce) with their supervisor to reflect on their learning journey, the research process, and the outcomes of their work.

nodes.name: RPPF 反思表
nodes.subject: ee
nodes.definition: Students will complete all three mandatory reflections on the official RPPF, using the form to document their engagement with the research process and their intellectual and personal development.
key_concepts: Students will complete all three mandatory reflections on the official RPPF, using the form to document their engagement with the research process and their intellectual and personal development.

nodes.name: 理科 EE 要点
nodes.subject: ee
nodes.definition: Students undertaking a Science EE will design and conduct a safe and ethically sound investigation, collecting and processing primary or secondary data to explore a specific scientific question.
key_concepts: Students undertaking a Science EE will design and conduct a safe and ethically sound investigation, collecting and processing primary or secondary data to explore a specific scientific question.
Students will analyze their results using appropriate scientific methods and techniques, discussing their significance in relation to established scientific theory and the research question.

nodes.name: 文科 EE 要点
nodes.subject: ee
nodes.definition: Students undertaking a Humanities EE (e.g., History, Economics, Psychology) will construct a critical argument based on the systematic analysis and evaluation of primary and secondary sources.
key_concepts: Students undertaking a Humanities EE (e.g., History, Economics, Psychology) will construct a critical argument based on the systematic analysis and evaluation of primary and secondary sources.
Students will demonstrate an understanding of the theoretical frameworks and historiographical or disciplinary debates relevant to their chosen topic.

nodes.name: 数学 EE 要点
nodes.subject: ee
nodes.definition: Students undertaking a Mathematics EE will engage in the exploration of a specific mathematical topic, demonstrating rigorous and precise mathematical reasoning and communication.
key_concepts: Students undertaking a Mathematics EE will engage in the exploration of a specific mathematical topic, demonstrating rigorous and precise mathematical reasoning and communication.
The essay may involve applying mathematics to solve a problem, proving theorems, or analyzing mathematical models, with a clear emphasis on the beauty and utility of mathematics itself.

nodes.name: 世界研究 EE
nodes.subject: ee
nodes.definition: Students undertaking a World Studies EE will formulate a research question of contemporary global significance that examines an issue through the lens of at least two IB disciplines.
key_concepts: Students undertaking a World Studies EE will formulate a research question of contemporary global significance that examines an issue through the lens of at least two IB disciplines.
Students will integrate concepts, theories, and methods from their chosen disciplines to construct a coherent interdisciplinary analysis of the complex global issue.

nodes.name: 文本细读
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students will be able to perform a detailed, line-by-line analysis of a literary or non-literary text, identifying and interpreting the effects of specific word choices, imagery, and syntax.
key_concepts: Students will be able to perform a detailed, line-by-line analysis of a literary or non-literary text, identifying and interpreting the effects of specific word choices, imagery, and syntax.
Students will be able to construct a coherent interpretation of a text's local meaning and overall significance based on sustained attention to textual detail.

nodes.name: 文学分析
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students will be able to formulate a clear, arguable thesis about a literary work's meaning, supported by well-chosen textual evidence and logical reasoning.
key_concepts: Students will be able to formulate a clear, arguable thesis about a literary work's meaning, supported by well-chosen textual evidence and logical reasoning.
Students will be able to evaluate how various literary elements (e.g., character, setting, theme, structure) interact to shape a work's overall impact and meaning.

nodes.name: 叙事技巧
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students will be able to analyse and evaluate the function of narrative point of view, voice, focalization, and temporal structure in shaping meaning and reader response in prose fiction.
key_concepts: Students will be able to analyse and evaluate the function of narrative point of view, voice, focalization, and temporal structure in shaping meaning and reader response in prose fiction.
Students will be able to explain how authors use techniques such as characterization, dialogue, and plot development to construct narrative and convey thematic concerns.

nodes.name: 诗歌分析
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students will be able to analyse the relationship between form (e.g., sonnet, free verse, stanzaic structure) and content in a poem, explaining how poetic techniques (meter, rhyme, enjambment) contribute to its meaning and effect.
key_concepts: Students will be able to analyse the relationship between form (e.g., sonnet, free verse, stanzaic structure) and content in a poem, explaining how poetic techniques (meter, rhyme, enjambment) contribute to its meaning and effect.
Students will be able to interpret complex imagery, metaphor, and symbolism in poetry, situating their analysis within the poem's broader thematic and emotional landscape.

nodes.name: 非文学文本
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students will be able to apply principles of textual analysis to a range of non-literary text types (e.g., advertisements, opinion columns, speeches, infographics), identifying their purpose, audience, and contextual constraints.
key_concepts: Students will be able to apply principles of textual analysis to a range of non-literary text types (e.g., advertisements, opinion columns, speeches, infographics), identifying their purpose, audience, and contextual constraints.
Students will be able to deconstruct the use of visual and linguistic design elements in non-literary texts to understand how they construct meaning and position the audience.

nodes.name: 创作语境
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students will be able to research and explain how the circumstances of a text's creation (author's background, historical events, publishing milieu, technological means) influence its form, content, and potential meanings.
key_concepts: Students will be able to research and explain how the circumstances of a text's creation (author's background, historical events, publishing milieu, technological means) influence its form, content, and potential meanings.

nodes.name: 接受语境
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students will be able to evaluate how different audiences, across time and culture, might receive and interpret a text differently, considering factors like ideology, social norms, and medium of consumption.
key_concepts: Students will be able to evaluate how different audiences, across time and culture, might receive and interpret a text differently, considering factors like ideology, social norms, and medium of consumption.

nodes.name: 文化语境
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students will be able to analyse how texts reflect, represent, or challenge the values, beliefs, and social practices of specific cultures or subcultures.
key_concepts: Students will be able to analyse how texts reflect, represent, or challenge the values, beliefs, and social practices of specific cultures or subcultures.
Students will be able to explore the role of texts in shaping cultural identity and negotiating cultural power dynamics.

nodes.name: 历史背景
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students will be able to situate a text within its specific historical period, drawing connections between its themes, style, or concerns and broader historical developments or intellectual movements of the era.
key_concepts: Students will be able to situate a text within its specific historical period, drawing connections between its themes, style, or concerns and broader historical developments or intellectual movements of the era.

nodes.name: 文体传统
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students will be able to identify the defining formal and thematic conventions of major literary genres (e.g., tragedy, satire, bildungsroman) and analyse how individual texts adhere to or subvert these conventions.
key_concepts: Students will be able to identify the defining formal and thematic conventions of major literary genres (e.g., tragedy, satire, bildungsroman) and analyse how individual texts adhere to or subvert these conventions.
Students will be able to classify non-literary texts by genre (e.g., editorial, manifesto, travel writing) and evaluate the strategic use of generic conventions to achieve a communicative purpose.

nodes.name: 比较研究
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students will be able to construct a focused, insightful comparison of two or more texts, moving beyond superficial similarities/differences to explore deeper connections in theme, technique, or context.
key_concepts: Students will be able to construct a focused, insightful comparison of two or more texts, moving beyond superficial similarities/differences to explore deeper connections in theme, technique, or context.
Students will be able to use comparison as a critical tool to illuminate the distinctive features and broader significance of each text in the pair or group.

nodes.name: 文学流派
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students will be able to define key characteristics of major literary movements (e.g., Romanticism, Modernism, Postcolonialism) and analyse how specific texts exemplify the aesthetic and philosophical principles of a movement.
key_concepts: Students will be able to define key characteristics of major literary movements (e.g., Romanticism, Modernism, Postcolonialism) and analyse how specific texts exemplify the aesthetic and philosophical principles of a movement.

nodes.name: IA 个人口头
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students will be able to deliver a structured, 10-minute oral presentation that analyses the relationship between a global issue and the content and form of one literary and one non-literary text.
key_concepts: Students will be able to deliver a structured, 10-minute oral presentation that analyses the relationship between a global issue and the content and form of one literary and one non-literary text.
Students will be able to engage in a thoughtful, spontaneous discussion with the teacher, demonstrating the ability to expand upon and defend their analysis in response to probing questions.

nodes.name: Paper 1 · 引导分析
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students will be able to write a coherent, analytical essay in response to an unseen literary or non-literary text, guided by a provided prompt, within a timed examination setting.
key_concepts: Students will be able to write a coherent, analytical essay in response to an unseen literary or non-literary text, guided by a provided prompt, within a timed examination setting.
Students will be able to select and analyse salient features of the text (both linguistic and stylistic), building a sustained argument that addresses the guiding question.

nodes.name: Paper 2 · 比较小论文
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students will be able to write a comparative essay, under timed conditions, in response to one of four general questions, drawing on their knowledge of at least two literary works studied in the course.
key_concepts: Students will be able to write a comparative essay, under timed conditions, in response to one of four general questions, drawing on their knowledge of at least two literary works studied in the course.
Students will be able to structure an essay that integrates comparison throughout, using relevant evidence from both works to develop a persuasive response to the chosen question.

nodes.name: HL 论文（4000词）
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students will be able to produce a formal, 1200-1500 word academic essay that develops a clear line of inquiry into a literary or non-literary text(s) studied in the course, demonstrating independent research and critical thinking.
key_concepts: Students will be able to produce a formal, 1200-1500 word academic essay that develops a clear line of inquiry into a literary or non-literary text(s) studied in the course, demonstrating independent research and critical thinking.

Students will be able to construct a sophisticated, sustained argument, supported by precise textual evidence and engagement with relevant scholarly sources, and presented with appropriate academic conventions.

nodes.name: 修辞手法
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students will be able to identify and analyse the strategic use of rhetorical devices (e.g., anaphora, antithesis, rhetorical questions) in both literary and non-literary texts, explaining their effect on the audience and contribution to the author's purpose.
key_concepts: Students will be able to identify and analyse the strategic use of rhetorical devices (e.g., anaphora, antithesis, rhetorical questions) in both literary and non-literary texts, explaining their effect on the audience and contribution to the author's purpose.

nodes.name: 语域与语气
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students will be able to analyse how variations in register (levels of formality, technicality) and tone (e.g., ironic, solemn, polemical) are constructed through diction, syntax, and modality to position the reader and shape meaning.
key_concepts: Students will be able to analyse how variations in register (levels of formality, technicality) and tone (e.g., ironic, solemn, polemical) are constructed through diction, syntax, and modality to position the reader and shape meaning.

nodes.name: 说服与修辞
nodes.subject: english
nodes.definition: Students will be able to deconstruct the persuasive strategies employed in argumentative texts, evaluating the use of logical appeals (logos), emotional appeals (pathos), and ethical appeals (ethos).
key_concepts: Students will be able to deconstruct the persuasive strategies employed in argumentative texts, evaluating the use of logical appeals (logos), emotional appeals (pathos), and ethical appeals (ethos).
Students will be able to analyse how texts seek to influence audience beliefs, attitudes, or behaviours, considering the interplay of argument, style, and context.

nodes.name: 第一次世界大战
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Students will be able to analyse the long-term and short-term causes of the First World War, evaluating the relative significance of factors such as militarism, alliances, imperialism, and nationalism (HL/SL).
key_concepts: Students will be able to analyse the long-term and short-term causes of the First World War, evaluating the relative significance of factors such as militarism, alliances, imperialism, and nationalism (HL/SL).
Students will be able to assess the social, economic, and political consequences of WWI, including the Treaty of Versailles and its impact on the post-war order.

nodes.name: 俄国革命
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Students will be able to explain the causes of the 1917 February and October Revolutions, evaluating the roles of the Tsarist regime, WWI, and revolutionary leadership (HL/SL).
key_concepts: Students will be able to explain the causes of the 1917 February and October Revolutions, evaluating the roles of the Tsarist regime, WWI, and revolutionary leadership (HL/SL).
Students will be able to compare and contrast the nature of the Provisional Government and the Bolshevik state under Lenin.

nodes.name: 战间期
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Students will be able to analyse the challenges to democracy and the rise of authoritarian states in the interwar period, using specific case studies (HL/SL).
key_concepts: Students will be able to analyse the challenges to democracy and the rise of authoritarian states in the interwar period, using specific case studies (HL/SL).
Students will be able to evaluate the causes and consequences of the Great Depression on international relations and domestic politics.

nodes.name: 第二次世界大战
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Students will be able to assess the causes of WWII, analysing the role of appeasement, the failure of collective security, and the aggressive foreign policies of Germany, Italy, and Japan (HL/SL).
key_concepts: Students will be able to assess the causes of WWII, analysing the role of appeasement, the failure of collective security, and the aggressive foreign policies of Germany, Italy, and Japan (HL/SL).
Students will be able to evaluate the social, economic, and technological impact of total war on civilian populations.

nodes.name: 冷战
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Students will be able to explain the origins of the Cold War, analysing ideological, political, and economic differences between the superpowers (HL/SL).
key_concepts: Students will be able to explain the origins of the Cold War, analysing ideological, political, and economic differences between the superpowers (HL/SL).
Students will be able to compare and contrast the nature and impact of Cold War crises (e.g., Berlin, Cuba) and conflicts in different regions.

nodes.name: 非殖民化
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Students will be able to analyse the causes and processes of decolonization in two regions, evaluating the role of nationalist movements, colonial policies, and the Cold War (HL/SL).
key_concepts: Students will be able to analyse the causes and processes of decolonization in two regions, evaluating the role of nationalist movements, colonial policies, and the Cold War (HL/SL).
Students will be able to assess the challenges faced by newly independent states in the post-colonial period.

nodes.name: 希特勒统治下的德国
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Students will be able to evaluate the methods used by the Nazi regime to establish and maintain total control, including the use of terror, propaganda, and economic policies (HL/SL).
key_concepts: Students will be able to evaluate the methods used by the Nazi regime to establish and maintain total control, including the use of terror, propaganda, and economic policies (HL/SL).
Students will be able to analyse the ideological roots and implementation of Nazi racial and social policies, including the persecution of minorities and the Holocaust.

nodes.name: 斯大林的苏联
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Students will be able to assess the methods used by Stalin to consolidate power, including political purges, show trials, and the cult of personality (HL/SL).
key_concepts: Students will be able to assess the methods used by Stalin to consolidate power, including political purges, show trials, and the cult of personality (HL/SL).
Students will be able to evaluate the economic and social impact of Stalin's policies, including collectivization, the Five-Year Plans, and the Great Terror.

nodes.name: 毛泽东时代的中国
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Students will be able to analyse the methods used by Mao Zedong to consolidate power in China, including ideological campaigns and mass mobilization (HL/SL).
key_concepts: Students will be able to analyse the methods used by Mao Zedong to consolidate power in China, including ideological campaigns and mass mobilization (HL/SL).
Students will be able to evaluate the social and economic impact of Mao's domestic policies, such as the Great Leap Forward and the Cultural Revolution.

nodes.name: 卡斯特罗的古巴
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Students will be able to explain the causes of the Cuban Revolution and evaluate the methods used by Fidel Castro to establish and maintain power (HL/SL).
key_concepts: Students will be able to explain the causes of the Cuban Revolution and evaluate the methods used by Fidel Castro to establish and maintain power (HL/SL).
Students will be able to assess the impact of Castro's domestic policies and Cuba's relationship with the superpowers during the Cold War.

nodes.name: 一手史料
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Students will be able to extract and record relevant information from a variety of primary sources, demonstrating comprehension of their explicit meaning (HL/SL).
key_concepts: Students will be able to extract and record relevant information from a variety of primary sources, demonstrating comprehension of their explicit meaning (HL/SL).
Students will be able to identify the origin, purpose, and content of primary sources as part of source analysis.

nodes.name: 史料评估（OPVL）
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Students will be able to evaluate the value and limitations of historical sources, with reference to their origin, purpose, and content (HL/SL, Paper 1 skill).
key_concepts: Students will be able to evaluate the value and limitations of historical sources, with reference to their origin, purpose, and content (HL/SL, Paper 1 skill).
Students will be able to analyse the tone, perspective, and argument presented in a source, placing it in its historical context.

nodes.name: 史学观点比较
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Students will be able to compare and contrast the arguments, perspectives, and methodologies of different historians on a specific historical issue (HL/SL).
key_concepts: Students will be able to compare and contrast the arguments, perspectives, and methodologies of different historians on a specific historical issue (HL/SL).
Students will be able to explain how and why historical interpretations differ over time.

nodes.name: 历史争鸣
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Students will be able to construct a sustained argument that engages with historical debate, using evidence to support their analysis (HL/SL, Paper 2/3 skill).
key_concepts: Students will be able to construct a sustained argument that engages with historical debate, using evidence to support their analysis (HL/SL, Paper 2/3 skill).
Students will be able to evaluate the relative merits of different historical interpretations in forming their own reasoned conclusion.

nodes.name: IA 历史探究
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Students will be able to formulate a clear, focused research question for an historical investigation on a topic of their choice (HL/SL Internal Assessment).
key_concepts: Students will be able to formulate a clear, focused research question for an historical investigation on a topic of their choice (HL/SL Internal Assessment).
Students will be able to critically analyse a range of sources and historical perspectives in their investigation, leading to a substantiated conclusion.

nodes.name: Paper 1 · 史料题
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Students will be able to analyse and evaluate primary sources in response to structured questions, demonstrating understanding of origin, purpose, value, and limitation (HL/SL Exam).
key_concepts: Students will be able to analyse and evaluate primary sources in response to structured questions, demonstrating understanding of origin, purpose, value, and limitation (HL/SL Exam).
Students will be able to synthesize information from multiple sources to construct a coherent short-term response.

nodes.name: Paper 2 · 专题论文
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Students will be able to construct two well-structured, analytical essays in response to prompts from two different world history topics (HL/SL Exam).
key_concepts: Students will be able to construct two well-structured, analytical essays in response to prompts from two different world history topics (HL/SL Exam).
Students will be able to integrate specific, relevant historical evidence and explicit historiography to support a balanced argument.

nodes.name: Paper 3 · 区域专题（HL）
nodes.subject: history
nodes.definition: Students will be able to construct three in-depth, analytical essays on aspects of the history of a specific region, demonstrating detailed knowledge and conceptual understanding (HL Exam).
key_concepts: Students will be able to construct three in-depth, analytical essays on aspects of the history of a specific region, demonstrating detailed knowledge and conceptual understanding (HL Exam).
Students will be able to evaluate different historical perspectives and interpretations in their essays, showing awareness of historiographical debate.

key_concepts:
SL 2.1
Content
Different forms of the equation of a straight line.
Gradient; intercepts.
Lines with gradients m1 and m2
Parallel lines m1=m2.
Perpendicular lines m1×m2= −1.

SL 2.2
Content
Concept of a function, domain, range and graph.
Function notation, for example f(x), v(t), C(n).
The concept of a function as a mathematical model.
Informal concept that an inverse function reverses or undoes the effect of a function.
Inverse function as a reflection in the line y=x, and the notation f−1(x).

The graph of a function; its equation y= f(x).

Determine key features of graphs.

Arithmetic sequences and series.

Applications.

Applications.

Financial applications of geometric sequences and series:
• compound interest
• annual depreciation.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.definition:
SL 1.7
Content Guidance, clarification and syllabus links
Laws of exponents with rational exponents. \(\frac{1}{a^{m}} = \sqrt[m]{a}\), if \(m\) is even this refers to the positive root.
For example: \(16^{\frac{3}{4}} = 8\).
Laws of logarithms. \(y = a^{x} \Leftrightarrow x = \log_{a} y\); \(\log_{a} a = 1\), \(\log_{a} 1 = 0\),
\(\log_{a} xy = \log_{a} x + \log_{a} y\) \(a, y \in \mathbb{N}, x \in \mathbb{Z}\)
\(\log_{a} \frac{x}{y} = \log_{a} x - \log_{a} y\)
\(\log_{a} x^{m} = m \log_{a} x\)
Examples: \(\log_{2} 4^{3} = \log_{2} 64 = 6\), \(\log_{2} 8 + \log_{2} 3 = \log_{2} 24\)
\(\log_{3} \frac{10}{4} = \log_{3} 10 - \log_{3} 4\)
\(\log_{4} 3^{5} = 5 \log_{4} 3\)
Link to: logarithmic and exponential graphs (SL2.9)
Change of base of a logarithm. \(\log_{4} 7 = \frac{\ln 7}{\ln 4}\)
\(\log_{a} x = \frac{\log_{b} x}{\log_{b} a}\), for \(a, b, x > 0\) Examples: \(\log_{25} 125 = \frac{\log_{5} 125}{\log_{5} 25} (= \frac{3}{2})\)
Solving exponential equations, including using \(x\)
logarithms. Examples: \((\frac{1}{3})^{x} = 9^{x+1}\), \(2^{x-1} = 10\).
Link to: using logarithmic and exponential graphs
(SL2.9).

SL 1.6
Content Guidance, clarification and syllabus links
Simple deductive proof, numerical and algebraic; how to lay out a left-hand side to right-hand side (LHS to RHS) proof.
The symbols and notation for equality and identity.
LHS to RHS proofs require students to begin with the left-hand side expression and transform this using known algebraic steps into the expression on the right-hand side (or vice versa).
Example: Show that (x−3)2+5≡x2−6x+14.
Students will be expected to show how they can check a result including a check of their own results.

AHL 1.15
Content Guidance, clarification and syllabus links
Proof by mathematical induction.
Proof should be incorporated throughout the course where appropriate.
Mathematical induction links specifically to a wide variety of topics, for example complex numbers, differentiation, sums of sequences and divisibility.
Proof by contradiction.
Examples: Irrationality of 3; irrationality of the cube root of 5; Euclid’s proof of an infinite number of prime numbers; if a is a rational number and b is an irrational number, then a+b is an irrational number.
Use of a counterexample to show that a statement is not always true.
Example: Consider the set P of numbers of the form n2+41n+41, n∈ℕ, show that not all elements of P are prime.
Example: Show that the following statement is not always true: there are no positive integer solutions to the equation x2+y2=10.
It is not sufficient to state the counterexample alone. Students must explain why their example is a counterexample.

Sketch and interpret graphs of exponential and logarithmic functions, identifying key features such as asymptotes and intercepts.

nodes.name: 矩阵（HL）

nodes.name: 回归与拟合

nodes.name: 三维几何

nodes.name: 三角应用

nodes.name: 图论（HL）

nodes.name: 描述统计

nodes.name: 相关与回归
