A.1 Kinematics
Guidance
A quantitative approach to projectile motion will be limited to situations where fluid resistance is absent or can be neglected.
The trajectory of projectile motion is parabolic in the absence of fluid resistance, but the equation of the trajectory is not required.
Familiarity with projectiles launched horizontally, at angles above, and at angles below the horizontal is required.
Projectile motion will only involve problems using a constant value of g close to the surface of the Earth.
Fluid resistance refers to the effects of gases and liquids on the motion of a body.

How can the motion of a mass in a gravitational field compare to the motion of a charged particle in an electric field?

Skill Description
Applying general mathematics • Use basic arithmetic and algebraic calculations to solve problems.
• Calculate areas and volumes for simple shapes.
• Carry out calculations involving decimals, fractions, percentages, ratios, reciprocals, exponents and trigonometric ratios.
• Carry out calculations involving logarithmic and exponential functions.
• Determine rates of change.
• Calculate mean and range.
• Use and interpret scientific notation (for example, 3.5 × 106).
• Select and manipulate equations.
• Derive relationships algebraically.
• Use approximation and estimation.
• Appreciate when some effects can be neglected and why this is useful.
• Compare and quote ratios, values and approximations to the nearest order of magnitude.
• Distinguish between continuous and discrete variables.
• Understand direct and inverse proportionality, as well as positive and negative relationships or correlations between variables.
• Determine the effect of changes to variables on other variables in a relationship.
• Calculate and interpret percentage change and percentage difference.
• Calculate and interpret percentage error and percentage uncertainty.
• Construct and use scale diagrams.
• Identify a quantity as a scalar or vector.

Skill Description
Graphing • Sketch graphs, with labelled but unscaled axes, to qualitatively describe trends.
• Construct and interpret tables, charts and graphs for raw and processed data including bar charts, pie charts, histograms, scatter graphs and line and curve graphs.
• Construct and interpret graphs using logarithmic scales.
• Plot linear and non-linear graphs showing the relationship between two variables with appropriate scales and axes.
• Draw lines or curves of best fit.
• Draw and interpret uncertainty bars.
• Extrapolate and interpolate graphs.
• Linearize graphs (only where appropriate).
• On a best-fit linear graph, construct lines of maximum and minimum gradients with relative accuracy (by eye) considering all uncertainty bars.
• Determining the uncertainty in gradients and intercepts.
• Interpret features of graphs including gradient, changes in gradient, intercepts, maxima and minima, and areas under the graph.

nodes.name: 知者视角
nodes.subject: tok
nodes.definition: Students will be able to analyse the role of personal and shared knowledge, and evaluate how factors such as emotion, reason, and culture shape the knower's perspective.
key_concepts: Students will be able to analyse the role of personal and shared knowledge, and evaluate how factors such as emotion, reason, and culture shape the knower's perspective.
Students will be able to reflect on their own perspectives as knowers and identify how their position in the world influences their understanding and claims.

nodes.name: 知识声明
nodes.subject: tok
nodes.definition: Students will be able to distinguish between shared and personal knowledge claims, and construct meaningful knowledge questions that arise from them.
key_concepts: Students will be able to distinguish between shared and personal knowledge claims, and construct meaningful knowledge questions that arise from them.
Students will be able to evaluate the implications of asserting 'I know' versus 'I believe' in different contexts.

nodes.name: 真理与信念
nodes.subject: tok
nodes.definition: Students will be able to compare and contrast theories of truth (e.g., correspondence, coherence, pragmatic) and analyse their applicability in different Areas of Knowledge.
key_concepts: Students will be able to compare and contrast theories of truth (e.g., correspondence, coherence, pragmatic) and analyse their applicability in different Areas of Knowledge.
Students will be able to critically examine the relationship between justification, evidence, belief, and truth.

nodes.name: 自然科学
nodes.subject: tok
nodes.definition: Students will be able to evaluate the roles of observation, experimentation, and falsification in the construction of scientific knowledge, considering the provisional nature of scientific claims.
key_concepts: Students will be able to evaluate the roles of observation, experimentation, and falsification in the construction of scientific knowledge, considering the provisional nature of scientific claims.
Students will be able to analyse how paradigms, models, and technological advances shape the methods and scope of the natural sciences.

nodes.name: 人文科学
nodes.subject: tok
nodes.definition: Students will be able to assess the methodological challenges in the human sciences, such as the role of interpretation, the observer effect, and the difficulty of establishing causal laws.
key_concepts: Students will be able to assess the methodological challenges in the human sciences, such as the role of interpretation, the observer effect, and the difficulty of establishing causal laws.
Students will be able to compare the nature of evidence and explanation in the human sciences with that in the natural sciences.

nodes.name: 历史
nodes.subject: tok
nodes.definition: Students will be able to analyse how historians construct knowledge through the selection, interpretation, and synthesis of evidence from the past.
key_concepts: Students will be able to analyse how historians construct knowledge through the selection, interpretation, and synthesis of evidence from the past.
Students will be able to evaluate the challenges of historical objectivity, including the role of perspective, bias, and the influence of present values on historical narratives.

nodes.name: 数学
nodes.subject: tok
nodes.definition: Students will be able to explain the roles of axiomatic systems, deductive reasoning, and proof in establishing mathematical certainty and truth.
key_concepts: Students will be able to explain the roles of axiomatic systems, deductive reasoning, and proof in establishing mathematical certainty and truth.
Students will be able to discuss the relationship between abstract mathematical concepts and their application in the real world, considering whether mathematics is discovered or invented.

nodes.name: 艺术
nodes.subject: tok
nodes.definition: Students will be able to analyse the role of imagination, emotion, and perception in the creation and interpretation of artistic knowledge.
key_concepts: Students will be able to analyse the role of imagination, emotion, and perception in the creation and interpretation of artistic knowledge.
Students will be able to evaluate different criteria used to judge artistic value and knowledge, considering the tension between subjective interpretation and objective standards.

nodes.name: 技术与知识
nodes.subject: tok
nodes.definition: Students will be able to analyse the impact of technological tools and media on the production, acquisition, and dissemination of knowledge across various AOKs.
key_concepts: Students will be able to analyse the impact of technological tools and media on the production, acquisition, and dissemination of knowledge across various AOKs.
Students will be able to evaluate ethical considerations and the potential for bias inherent in the algorithms and design of knowledge technologies.

nodes.name: 语言与知识
nodes.subject: tok
nodes.definition: Students will be able to analyse how language shapes thought, classification, and the communication of knowledge within and between communities.
key_concepts: Students will be able to analyse how language shapes thought, classification, and the communication of knowledge within and between communities.
Students will be able to evaluate the challenges of translation, ambiguity, and the use of metaphor in the pursuit of precise knowledge.

nodes.name: 政治与知识
nodes.subject: tok
nodes.definition: Students will be able to analyse how power structures and ideologies influence the production, validation, and control of knowledge within societies.
key_concepts: Students will be able to analyse how power structures and ideologies influence the production, validation, and control of knowledge within societies.
Students will be able to evaluate the concept of 'official knowledge' and the role of education, media, and institutions in shaping public understanding.

nodes.name: 宗教与知识
nodes.subject: tok
nodes.definition: Students will be able to compare the nature of faith-based knowledge claims with those based on evidence and reason, analysing their different foundations and methods of justification.
key_concepts: Students will be able to compare the nature of faith-based knowledge claims with those based on evidence and reason, analysing their different foundations and methods of justification.
Students will be able to discuss the role of religious knowledge systems in providing frameworks for understanding the world and human experience.

nodes.name: 本土社会
nodes.subject: tok
nodes.definition: Students will be able to analyse distinctive features of indigenous knowledge systems, such as holistic perspectives, oral tradition, and connections to land and community.
key_concepts: Students will be able to analyse distinctive features of indigenous knowledge systems, such as holistic perspectives, oral tradition, and connections to land and community.
Students will be able to reflect on the implications of different knowledge systems for understanding issues of sustainability, identity, and cultural preservation.

nodes.name: TOK 展览（IA）
nodes.subject: tok
nodes.definition: Students will be able to select a prescribed title and curate an exhibition of three objects that effectively explore knowledge questions arising from it in a concrete, real-world context.
key_concepts: Students will be able to select a prescribed title and curate an exhibition of three objects that effectively explore knowledge questions arising from it in a concrete, real-world context.
Students will be able to produce a written commentary that clearly justifies the selection of each object and explains its specific connection to the chosen title and relevant TOK concepts.

nodes.name: TOK Essay（1600 词）
nodes.subject: tok
nodes.definition: Students will be able to construct a focused, coherent, and critical argument in response to a prescribed essay title, integrating analysis of specific Areas of Knowledge and relevant TOK concepts.
key_concepts: Students will be able to construct a focused, coherent, and critical argument in response to a prescribed essay title, integrating analysis of specific Areas of Knowledge and relevant TOK concepts.
Students will be able to demonstrate independent thinking, precise use of TOK terminology, and effective evaluation of competing perspectives and implications in their essay.

nodes.name: 素描与观察
nodes.subject: art
nodes.definition: Students in MYP years 1-3 will be able to employ a range of drawing techniques (e.g., contour, gesture, tonal rendering) to accurately represent form, space, and proportion.
key_concepts: Students in MYP years 1-3 will be able to employ a range of drawing techniques (e.g., contour, gesture, tonal rendering) to accurately represent form, space, and proportion.
Students in MYP years 4-5 will be able to select and refine drawing skills purposefully to develop a personal visual language and support artistic intention in their body of work.

nodes.name: 绘画媒材
nodes.subject: art
nodes.definition: Students will be able to demonstrate technical competence in applying various painting media (e.g., watercolor, acrylic, gouache) to explore color theory, texture, and compositional effects.
key_concepts: Students will be able to demonstrate technical competence in applying various painting media (e.g., watercolor, acrylic, gouache) to explore color theory, texture, and compositional effects.
Students will be able to make informed choices about painting materials and techniques to convey specific moods, concepts, or cultural contexts in their artwork.

nodes.name: 雕塑与立体
nodes.subject: art
nodes.definition: Students in MYP years 2-4 will be able to manipulate a variety of materials (e.g., clay, wire, found objects) using additive, subtractive, and construction techniques to create three-dimensional forms.
key_concepts: Students in MYP years 2-4 will be able to manipulate a variety of materials (e.g., clay, wire, found objects) using additive, subtractive, and construction techniques to create three-dimensional forms.
Students will be able to apply an understanding of spatial relationships, scale, and structural integrity to design and realize sculptural artworks.

nodes.name: 版画
nodes.subject: art
nodes.definition: Students will be able to execute basic printmaking processes (e.g., relief, monotype) to produce multiple images, demonstrating an understanding of registration, inking, and editioning.
key_concepts: Students will be able to execute basic printmaking processes (e.g., relief, monotype) to produce multiple images, demonstrating an understanding of registration, inking, and editioning.
Students will be able to utilize the unique qualities of printmaking (e.g., repetition, variation) to explore pattern, sequence, or social commentary in their visual communication.

nodes.name: 数字媒体
nodes.subject: art
nodes.definition: Students in MYP years 3-5 will be able to use digital tools and software for creating, manipulating, and presenting still and moving images, demonstrating digital literacy.
key_concepts: Students in MYP years 3-5 will be able to use digital tools and software for creating, manipulating, and presenting still and moving images, demonstrating digital literacy.
Students will be able to critically evaluate the role of digital media in contemporary art practice and society, applying this understanding to their own creative projects.

nodes.name: 艺术史
nodes.subject: art
nodes.definition: Students will be able to identify and analyze key artworks, movements, and cultural contexts from different historical periods and global traditions.
key_concepts: Students will be able to identify and analyze key artworks, movements, and cultural contexts from different historical periods and global traditions.
Students will be able to investigate the connections between art historical knowledge and their own artistic development, using research to inform and contextualize their work.

nodes.name: 识谱
nodes.subject: art
nodes.definition: Students in MYP years 1-3 will be able to interpret and apply standard musical notation (pitch, rhythm, dynamics, articulation) in performance and composition tasks.
key_concepts: Students in MYP years 1-3 will be able to interpret and apply standard musical notation (pitch, rhythm, dynamics, articulation) in performance and composition tasks.
Students in MYP years 4-5 will be able to fluently read and notate musical ideas using appropriate conventions, facilitating collaboration and analysis.

nodes.name: 乐器演奏
nodes.subject: art
nodes.definition: Students will be able to develop technical proficiency on a chosen instrument or voice, demonstrating control over tone, intonation, and expressive techniques.
key_concepts: Students will be able to develop technical proficiency on a chosen instrument or voice, demonstrating control over tone, intonation, and expressive techniques.
Students will be able to perform repertoire from diverse genres and cultures with stylistic awareness, both as a soloist and as part of an ensemble.

nodes.name: 创作与编曲
nodes.subject: art
nodes.definition: Students will be able to create original musical pieces by structuring and developing musical ideas (melody, rhythm, harmony, texture) using appropriate tools and technology.
key_concepts: Students will be able to create original musical pieces by structuring and developing musical ideas (melody, rhythm, harmony, texture) using appropriate tools and technology.
Students will be able to apply knowledge of musical elements and structures to compose for specific purposes, audiences, or contexts, and reflect on their creative process.

nodes.name: 音乐体裁
nodes.subject: art
nodes.definition: Students will be able to identify and describe the distinguishing characteristics, cultural origins, and historical development of a range of musical genres.
key_concepts: Students will be able to identify and describe the distinguishing characteristics, cultural origins, and historical development of a range of musical genres.
Students will be able to compare and contrast musical genres, evaluating how social, historical, and technological factors influence musical style and practice.

nodes.name: 表演基础
nodes.subject: art
nodes.definition: Students in MYP years 1-2 will be able to apply fundamental acting techniques (e.g., vocal projection, physical characterization, focus) in prepared and improvised scenarios.
key_concepts: Students in MYP years 1-2 will be able to apply fundamental acting techniques (e.g., vocal projection, physical characterization, focus) in prepared and improvised scenarios.
Students will be able to use voice, movement, and gesture intentionally to create believable characters and communicate clear intentions on stage.

nodes.name: 剧目排练
nodes.subject: art
nodes.definition: Students in MYP years 3-5 will be able to analyze a scripted scene to make directorial and performance choices regarding character motivation, relationship, and staging.
key_concepts: Students in MYP years 3-5 will be able to analyze a scripted scene to make directorial and performance choices regarding character motivation, relationship, and staging.
Students will be able to collaborate effectively within an ensemble to rehearse, refine, and perform scenes, demonstrating responsiveness and stagecraft.

nodes.name: 戏剧史
nodes.subject: art
nodes.definition: Students will be able to trace the development of theatrical forms, conventions, and practitioners from classical traditions to contemporary practice.
key_concepts: Students will be able to trace the development of theatrical forms, conventions, and practitioners from classical traditions to contemporary practice.
Students will be able to investigate how theatre reflects and influences the society and culture in which it is created, and apply this understanding to their own dramatic work.

nodes.name: 艺术家研究
nodes.subject: art
nodes.definition: Students will be able to conduct in-depth research into the life, influences, techniques, and body of work of a selected artist, musician, or theatre practitioner.
key_concepts: Students will be able to conduct in-depth research into the life, influences, techniques, and body of work of a selected artist, musician, or theatre practitioner.
Students will be able to critically analyze the work of studied practitioners to evaluate their impact and relevance, and draw connections to their own artistic practice.

nodes.name: 艺术评论
nodes.subject: art
nodes.definition: Students will be able to use appropriate arts terminology to describe, analyze, interpret, and evaluate artworks and performances (their own and others').
key_concepts: Students will be able to use appropriate arts terminology to describe, analyze, interpret, and evaluate artworks and performances (their own and others').
Students will be able to engage constructively in critique sessions, providing and applying feedback to refine artistic work in relation to stated intentions and criteria.

nodes.name: 过程日志
nodes.subject: art
nodes.definition: Students will be able to document their artistic process, research, experimentation, and reflections consistently in a journal, demonstrating the development of ideas over time.
key_concepts: Students will be able to document their artistic process, research, experimentation, and reflections consistently in a journal, demonstrating the development of ideas over time.
Students will use the process journal to plan, record, and evaluate their work against the MYP Arts criteria, showing evidence of critical thinking and artistic growth.

nodes.name: 探究与分析
nodes.subject: design
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to formulate a detailed design brief by identifying and analysing a need for a specific client or target audience.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to formulate a detailed design brief by identifying and analysing a need for a specific client or target audience.
Students in MYP 4-5 will be able to conduct and synthesize research from a range of primary and secondary sources to inform the development of a design specification.

nodes.name: 构思与方案
nodes.subject: design
nodes.definition: Students will be able to generate a range of feasible design ideas, using techniques such as annotation and sketching, that address the specifications outlined in the design brief.
key_concepts: Students will be able to generate a range of feasible design ideas, using techniques such as annotation and sketching, that address the specifications outlined in the design brief.
Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to develop detailed planning drawings/diagrams and justify the selection of one final design against the specification.

nodes.name: 制作解决方案
nodes.subject: design
nodes.definition: Students will be able to competently use a range of techniques and equipment to construct a logical plan and create a high-quality prototype or product.
key_concepts: Students will be able to competently use a range of techniques and equipment to construct a logical plan and create a high-quality prototype or product.
Students in MYP 2-5 will demonstrate technical skill and safety in the use of tools and materials, documenting the creation process with photographic evidence.

nodes.name: 评估与迭代
nodes.subject: design
nodes.definition: Students will be able to test their final product/solution against the original design specification and explain the success and limitations of the outcome.
key_concepts: Students will be able to test their final product/solution against the original design specification and explain the success and limitations of the outcome.
Students in MYP 4-5 will be able to critically evaluate the impact of their solution on the client/target audience and propose detailed, realistic modifications for improvement.

nodes.name: 网页基础（HTML/CSS）
nodes.subject: design
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to explain the core components of web architecture (e.g., HTML, CSS, servers) and create a simple, functional multi-page website using basic tags and styling.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to explain the core components of web architecture (e.g., HTML, CSS, servers) and create a simple, functional multi-page website using basic tags and styling.
Students in MYP 4-5 will be able to design and develop a website that follows principles of user-centered design and digital accessibility.

nodes.name: 编程入门
nodes.subject: design
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to use visual or text-based programming environments to create simple algorithms that solve defined problems, using constructs such as sequences, loops, and conditionals.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to use visual or text-based programming environments to create simple algorithms that solve defined problems, using constructs such as sequences, loops, and conditionals.
Students in MYP 4-5 will be able to design, write, debug, and document a functional program to address a specific need within a design project.

nodes.name: 用户界面设计
nodes.subject: design
nodes.definition: Students will be able to apply fundamental principles of user interface design (e.g., consistency, hierarchy, feedback) to develop low-fidelity wireframes for a digital product.
key_concepts: Students will be able to apply fundamental principles of user interface design (e.g., consistency, hierarchy, feedback) to develop low-fidelity wireframes for a digital product.
Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to justify their UI design choices in relation to the needs and characteristics of a specific user group.

nodes.name: 用户测试
nodes.subject: design
nodes.definition: Students will be able to plan and conduct simple user tests to gather qualitative and quantitative feedback on a prototype.
key_concepts: Students will be able to plan and conduct simple user tests to gather qualitative and quantitative feedback on a prototype.
Students in MYP 4-5 will be able to analyse user testing data, identify patterns, and translate findings into specific design modifications.

nodes.name: 设计草图
nodes.subject: design
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to use freehand sketching techniques, including annotation, to communicate design ideas and explore form.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to use freehand sketching techniques, including annotation, to communicate design ideas and explore form.
Students in MYP 4-5 will be able to produce annotated, rendered sketches that effectively communicate aesthetic and functional details of a proposed solution.

nodes.name: 原型制作
nodes.subject: design
nodes.definition: Students will be able to construct a physical or digital prototype that models key features of their final design idea for the purpose of testing and evaluation.
key_concepts: Students will be able to construct a physical or digital prototype that models key features of their final design idea for the purpose of testing and evaluation.
Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to select and justify appropriate prototyping methods (e.g., paper, 3D print, digital mock-up) based on the design context and testing goals.

nodes.name: 材料与工具
nodes.subject: design
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to identify and describe the working properties of common materials (e.g., wood, polymers, textiles) and select appropriate tools for basic processing.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to identify and describe the working properties of common materials (e.g., wood, polymers, textiles) and select appropriate tools for basic processing.
Students in MYP 4-5 will be able to justify their selection of specific materials, components, and tools based on functional requirements, availability, cost, and environmental impact.

nodes.name: CAD 入门
nodes.subject: design
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 2-4 will be able to use basic CAD software tools to create and modify simple 2D drawings and 3D digital models.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 2-4 will be able to use basic CAD software tools to create and modify simple 2D drawings and 3D digital models.
Students in MYP 5 will be able to produce a set of annotated CAD drawings suitable for guiding the manufacture of a prototype, applying scale and dimensioning conventions.

nodes.name: 用户研究
nodes.subject: design
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to use simple methods (e.g., surveys, interviews, observation) to gather information about user needs and preferences.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to use simple methods (e.g., surveys, interviews, observation) to gather information about user needs and preferences.
Students in MYP 4-5 will be able to synthesize findings from user research to create detailed user personas and scenarios that drive the design specification.

nodes.name: 设计规范书
nodes.subject: design
nodes.definition: Students will be able to develop a design specification with a list of clear, measurable criteria derived from the analysis of their design brief and research.
key_concepts: Students will be able to develop a design specification with a list of clear, measurable criteria derived from the analysis of their design brief and research.
Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to prioritize specification criteria and justify how they address the needs of the client and the requirements of the problem.

nodes.name: 伦理与可持续
nodes.subject: design
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to identify ethical and environmental considerations (e.g., sourcing, waste, inclusivity) relevant to a design context.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to identify ethical and environmental considerations (e.g., sourcing, waste, inclusivity) relevant to a design context.
Students in MYP 4-5 will be able to critically evaluate a design solution's social and environmental impact and propose modifications that align with principles of sustainable design.

nodes.name: 古代文明
nodes.subject: humanities
nodes.definition: Analyze the causes and consequences of the rise and fall of ancient civilizations, evaluating their enduring legacies on contemporary societies (AO2, AO3).
key_concepts: Analyze the causes and consequences of the rise and fall of ancient civilizations, evaluating their enduring legacies on contemporary societies (AO2, AO3).
Investigate the social, political, and economic structures of selected ancient civilizations using primary and secondary sources to develop historical arguments (AO1, AO2).

nodes.name: 中世纪世界
nodes.subject: humanities
nodes.definition: Evaluate the significance of social, religious, and political systems (e.g., feudalism, manorialism) in shaping medieval societies across different regions (AO3).
key_concepts: Evaluate the significance of social, religious, and political systems (e.g., feudalism, manorialism) in shaping medieval societies across different regions (AO3).
Assess the causes and effects of cross-cultural interactions and conflicts during the medieval period, such as the Crusades or the Silk Road exchanges (AO2).

nodes.name: 工业革命
nodes.subject: humanities
nodes.definition: Analyze the complex causes and global consequences of the Industrial Revolution, evaluating its social, economic, and environmental impacts (AO2, AO3).
key_concepts: Analyze the complex causes and global consequences of the Industrial Revolution, evaluating its social, economic, and environmental impacts (AO2, AO3).
Investigate primary sources to construct arguments about the experiences of different social groups during the period of industrialization (AO1, AO2).

nodes.name: 两次世界大战
nodes.subject: humanities
nodes.definition: Evaluate the interplay of long-term and short-term causes of the World Wars, and assess their geopolitical, social, and technological consequences (AO3).
key_concepts: Evaluate the interplay of long-term and short-term causes of the World Wars, and assess their geopolitical, social, and technological consequences (AO3).
Use a variety of historical sources to analyze different perspectives on the conduct and experience of total war, developing critical interpretations (AO1, AO2).

nodes.name: 冷战
nodes.subject: humanities
nodes.definition: Analyze the ideological, political, and economic origins of the Cold War, and evaluate its manifestation as a global conflict through proxy wars and spheres of influence (AO2, AO3).
key_concepts: Analyze the ideological, political, and economic origins of the Cold War, and evaluate its manifestation as a global conflict through proxy wars and spheres of influence (AO2, AO3).
Investigate the social and cultural impacts of the Cold War on different nations and groups, using source analysis to support conclusions (AO1, AO3).

nodes.name: 史料分析
nodes.subject: humanities
nodes.definition: Demonstrate the ability to critically evaluate the origin, purpose, value, and limitation (OPVL) of different types of historical sources (AO1).
key_concepts: Demonstrate the ability to critically evaluate the origin, purpose, value, and limitation (OPVL) of different types of historical sources (AO1).
Synthesize information from multiple, often conflicting, sources to construct well-supported historical narratives and arguments (AO2).

nodes.name: 自然地理
nodes.subject: humanities
nodes.definition: Explain how natural processes shape the physical characteristics of landscapes and environments, using geographic terminology and concepts (e.g., plate tectonics, geomorphological cycles) (AO1).
key_concepts: Explain how natural processes shape the physical characteristics of landscapes and environments, using geographic terminology and concepts (e.g., plate tectonics, geomorphological cycles) (AO1).
Analyze the complex interactions between physical geography and human activity, evaluating opportunities and constraints (AO2, AO3).

nodes.name: 人文地理
nodes.subject: humanities
nodes.definition: Investigate patterns and trends in human geography (e.g., cultural landscapes, economic activity, political organization) and explain the factors that produce them (AO1, AO2).
key_concepts: Investigate patterns and trends in human geography (e.g., cultural landscapes, economic activity, political organization) and explain the factors that produce them (AO1, AO2).
Evaluate the consequences of human geographic processes on places and populations at various scales (AO3).

key_concepts: Demonstrate proficiency in a range of manipulative skills (catching, throwing, striking, dribbling) with control and accuracy in isolated and applied settings, addressing Criterion D: Applying and Performing.

Adapt and transfer ball skills across different invasion, net/wall, and striking/fielding games, analyzing the similarities and differences in technique and application, which relates to Criterion C: Applying and Performing.

nodes.name: 团队运动
nodes.subject: pe
nodes.definition: Collaborate effectively within a team to apply strategies and tactics in an invasion game (e.g., basketball, soccer), demonstrating communication, role-specific responsibilities, and adherence to rules, as assessed in Criterion D: Applying and Performing.
key_concepts: Collaborate effectively within a team to apply strategies and tactics in an invasion game (e.g., basketball, soccer), demonstrating communication, role-specific responsibilities, and adherence to rules, as assessed in Criterion D: Applying and Performing.

Analyze the social and personal benefits of participating in team sports, evaluating how cooperation, leadership, and conflict resolution contribute to a positive group dynamic and personal development, linking to Criterion A: Knowing and Understanding.

nodes.name: 个人项目（田径/游泳）
nodes.subject: pe
nodes.definition: Develop and execute a performance plan for an individual sport (e.g., athletics, swimming, tennis), focusing on refining technique, setting personal goals, and applying self-assessment strategies, in line with Criterion B: Planning for Performance.
key_concepts: Develop and execute a performance plan for an individual sport (e.g., athletics, swimming, tennis), focusing on refining technique, setting personal goals, and applying self-assessment strategies, in line with Criterion B: Planning for Performance.

Compare and contrast the physiological and psychological demands of different individual sports, explaining how training principles and mental preparation are adapted for specific activities, which connects to Criterion A: Knowing and Understanding.

nodes.name: 体操
nodes.subject: pe
nodes.definition: Compose and perform a sequence on floor or apparatus that demonstrates creativity, fluency, and control, incorporating a variety of skills (travel, rotation, balance, flight) and linking movements, as per Criterion B: Movement Composition.
key_concepts: Compose and perform a sequence on floor or apparatus that demonstrates creativity, fluency, and control, incorporating a variety of skills (travel, rotation, balance, flight) and linking movements, as per Criterion B: Movement Composition.

Apply knowledge of safety principles, including spotting techniques and apparatus setup, while performing and analyzing gymnastic movements, demonstrating responsibility for self and others, assessed in Criterion D: Applying and Performing.

nodes.name: 体能训练
nodes.subject: pe
nodes.definition: Design, implement, and monitor a personal fitness training program based on the FITT principles (Frequency, Intensity, Time, Type) to achieve a specific health- or skill-related goal, demonstrating understanding of Criterion B: Planning for Performance.
key_concepts: Design, implement, and monitor a personal fitness training program based on the FITT principles (Frequency, Intensity, Time, Type) to achieve a specific health- or skill-related goal, demonstrating understanding of Criterion B: Planning for Performance.

Analyze the components of health-related fitness (cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility, body composition) and explain their interrelationship and importance for overall wellbeing, linking to Criterion A: Knowing and Understanding.

nodes.name: 攻守策略
nodes.subject: pe
nodes.definition: Apply offensive (e.g., creating space, penetration) and defensive (e.g., marking, zoning) principles in modified and full-sided games, adapting decisions in response to opponents' actions, as assessed in Criterion C: Applying and Performing.
key_concepts: Apply offensive (e.g., creating space, penetration) and defensive (e.g., marking, zoning) principles in modified and full-sided games, adapting decisions in response to opponents' actions, as assessed in Criterion C: Applying and Performing.

Compare and contrast offensive and defensive strategies across different game categories (invasion, net/wall), explaining the tactical rationale behind specific formations and movements, which relates to Criterion A: Knowing and Understanding.

nodes.name: 战术意识
nodes.subject: pe
nodes.definition: Demonstrate tactical awareness by selecting and applying appropriate strategies (e.g., width and depth in attack, delay in defense) to solve problems posed during game play, addressing Criterion C: Applying and Performing.
key_concepts: Demonstrate tactical awareness by selecting and applying appropriate strategies (e.g., width and depth in attack, delay in defense) to solve problems posed during game play, addressing Criterion C: Applying and Performing.

Evaluate the effectiveness of tactical decisions in a game situation, using terminology such as 'advantage' and 'transition' to analyze performance and propose improvements, linking to Criterion A: Knowing and Understanding.

nodes.name: 比赛分析
nodes.subject: pe
nodes.definition: Use systematic observation and notation to analyze the key components (skills, strategies, rules) of a game performance, identifying strengths and areas for improvement for an individual or team, as per Criterion A: Knowing and Understanding.
key_concepts: Use systematic observation and notation to analyze the key components (skills, strategies, rules) of a game performance, identifying strengths and areas for improvement for an individual or team, as per Criterion A: Knowing and Understanding.

Synthesize data from game analysis to formulate a detailed action plan for improving performance in a specific role or position, demonstrating the ability to apply findings, which connects to Criterion B: Planning for Performance.

nodes.name: 营养与饮食
nodes.subject: pe
nodes.definition: Explain the functions and sources of major nutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water) and analyze their role in supporting physical activity, health, and recovery, addressing Criterion A: Knowing and Understanding.
key_concepts: Explain the functions and sources of major nutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water) and analyze their role in supporting physical activity, health, and recovery, addressing Criterion A: Knowing and Understanding.

Critically evaluate personal dietary habits and create a nutrition plan that supports participation in a specific physical activity, considering energy requirements, hydration, and timing of intake, in line with Criterion B: Planning for Performance.

nodes.name: 心肺健康
nodes.subject: pe
nodes.definition: Investigate the structure and function of the cardiovascular system and explain the acute and long-term effects of exercise on heart rate, stroke volume, cardiac output, and blood pressure, linking to Criterion A: Knowing and Understanding.
key_concepts: Investigate the structure and function of the cardiovascular system and explain the acute and long-term effects of exercise on heart rate, stroke volume, cardiac output, and blood pressure, linking to Criterion A: Knowing and Understanding.

Design and participate in a training program aimed at improving cardiovascular endurance, using methods such as continuous training, interval training, and circuit training, and monitor progress using relevant data (e.g., resting heart rate, recovery rate), as assessed in Criterion B: Planning for Performance.

nodes.name: 心理健康
nodes.subject: pe
nodes.definition: They understand the importance of intellectual, physical and emotional balance to achieve personal well-being for themselves and others.
key_concepts: They understand the importance of intellectual, physical and emotional balance to achieve personal well-being for themselves and others.

nodes.name: 物质滥用防范
nodes.subject: pe
nodes.definition: Analyze the short- and long-term physical, social, and emotional effects of substance use (including alcohol, tobacco, and performance-enhancing drugs) on health, wellbeing, and athletic performance, addressing Criterion A: Knowing and Understanding.
key_concepts: Analyze the short- and long-term physical, social, and emotional effects of substance use (including alcohol, tobacco, and performance-enhancing drugs) on health, wellbeing, and athletic performance, addressing Criterion A: Knowing and Understanding.

Evaluate strategies for making informed, healthy choices regarding substance use and promote positive alternatives within a peer group or team setting, demonstrating an understanding of personal and social responsibility, which relates to Criterion D: Applying and Performing.

nodes.name: 目标设定
nodes.subject: pe
nodes.definition: They are able to assess and understand their strengths and limitations in order to support their learning and personal development.
key_concepts: They are able to assess and understand their strengths and limitations in order to support their learning and personal development.

nodes.name: 体育精神
nodes.subject: pe
nodes.definition: They act with integrity and honesty, with a strong sense of fairness, justice and respect for the dignity of the individual, groups and communities.
key_concepts: They act with integrity and honesty, with a strong sense of fairness, justice and respect for the dignity of the individual, groups and communities.

nodes.name: 自我评估
nodes.subject: pe
nodes.definition: They give thoughtful consideration to their own learning and experience. They are able to assess and understand their strengths and limitations in order to support their learning and personal development.
key_concepts: They give thoughtful consideration to their own learning and experience. They are able to assess and understand their strengths and limitations in order to support their learning and personal development.

nodes.name: 细胞结构与功能
nodes.subject: science
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to use a microscope to identify and describe the basic structures and functions of plant and animal cells, including the nucleus, cytoplasm, cell membrane, and chloroplasts.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to use a microscope to identify and describe the basic structures and functions of plant and animal cells, including the nucleus, cytoplasm, cell membrane, and chloroplasts.
Students will be able to explain the role of cells as the basic structural and functional units of living organisms, and describe the process of cellular division (mitosis) for growth and repair.

nodes.name: 人体系统
nodes.subject: science
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 2-4 will be able to describe the structure and function of at least two major human body systems (e.g., digestive, respiratory, circulatory) and explain how they interact to maintain health.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 2-4 will be able to describe the structure and function of at least two major human body systems (e.g., digestive, respiratory, circulatory) and explain how they interact to maintain health.
Students will be able to investigate a lifestyle factor (e.g., diet, exercise) and analyze its impact on the efficient functioning of a chosen body system.

nodes.name: 遗传入门
nodes.subject: science
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 3-4 will be able to define and use basic genetic terminology, including gene, allele, dominant, recessive, genotype, and phenotype.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 3-4 will be able to define and use basic genetic terminology, including gene, allele, dominant, recessive, genotype, and phenotype.
Students will be able to construct and interpret simple Punnett squares to predict the probability of inherited traits in offspring.

nodes.name: 进化入门
nodes.subject: science
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to explain the concept of natural selection as a mechanism for evolution, using specific examples of variation, adaptation, and environmental pressure.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to explain the concept of natural selection as a mechanism for evolution, using specific examples of variation, adaptation, and environmental pressure.
Students will be able to evaluate different types of evidence (e.g., fossil records, anatomical similarities) that support the theory of evolution.

nodes.name: 生态学
nodes.subject: science
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 1-4 will be able to construct and analyze food chains and webs to illustrate the flow of energy and interdependence of organisms within an ecosystem.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 1-4 will be able to construct and analyze food chains and webs to illustrate the flow of energy and interdependence of organisms within an ecosystem.
Students will be able to investigate an environmental factor (e.g., pH, temperature) and assess its impact on a specific population within a local ecosystem.

nodes.name: 物质与状态
nodes.subject: science
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to describe the arrangement, movement, and energy of particles in the three common states of matter (solid, liquid, gas).
key_concepts: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to describe the arrangement, movement, and energy of particles in the three common states of matter (solid, liquid, gas).
Students will be able to use the particle model to explain physical changes of state (e.g., melting, evaporation) in terms of energy transfer.

nodes.name: 原子与分子
nodes.subject: science
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 2-4 will be able to describe the basic structure of an atom (protons, neutrons, electrons) and use the periodic table to identify elements by their atomic number and mass.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 2-4 will be able to describe the basic structure of an atom (protons, neutrons, electrons) and use the periodic table to identify elements by their atomic number and mass.
Students will be able to differentiate between atoms, elements, molecules, and compounds, and represent simple molecules using chemical formulas (e.g., H2O, CO2).

nodes.name: 化学反应
nodes.subject: science
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to identify evidence of a chemical reaction (e.g., color change, gas production, temperature change) and distinguish it from a physical change.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to identify evidence of a chemical reaction (e.g., color change, gas production, temperature change) and distinguish it from a physical change.
Students will be able to write simple word equations and balanced chemical equations for common reactions, such as combustion or acid-metal reactions.

nodes.name: 酸碱
nodes.subject: science
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 3-4 will be able to use the pH scale to classify solutions as acidic, basic, or neutral, and safely use indicators to test common household substances.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 3-4 will be able to use the pH scale to classify solutions as acidic, basic, or neutral, and safely use indicators to test common household substances.
Students will be able to describe the properties of acids and bases, and explain the process of neutralization with examples from everyday life (e.g., indigestion remedies).

nodes.name: 力与运动
nodes.subject: science
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 2-4 will be able to calculate average speed using the formula speed = distance/time and represent motion graphically using distance-time graphs.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 2-4 will be able to calculate average speed using the formula speed = distance/time and represent motion graphically using distance-time graphs.
Students will be able to identify and describe different types of forces (e.g., friction, gravity, magnetic) and explain their effects on the motion of objects using Newton's First Law.

nodes.name: 能量
nodes.subject: science
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 1-4 will be able to identify different forms of energy (e.g., kinetic, potential, thermal, chemical) and describe energy transfers and transformations in simple systems.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 1-4 will be able to identify different forms of energy (e.g., kinetic, potential, thermal, chemical) and describe energy transfers and transformations in simple systems.
Students will be able to apply the principle of conservation of energy to explain that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only changed from one form to another.

nodes.name: 波动
nodes.subject: science
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to describe wave properties (wavelength, frequency, amplitude) and differentiate between transverse and longitudinal waves using examples like light and sound.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to describe wave properties (wavelength, frequency, amplitude) and differentiate between transverse and longitudinal waves using examples like light and sound.
Students will be able to explain how the properties of waves (e.g., reflection, refraction) are applied in technologies such as mirrors, lenses, or ultrasound imaging.

nodes.name: 电路与电磁
nodes.subject: science
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to construct simple series and parallel circuits using schematic diagrams and explain the effect of adding components on current and brightness.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to construct simple series and parallel circuits using schematic diagrams and explain the effect of adding components on current and brightness.
Students will be able to describe the relationship between magnetism and electricity, and explain the principle of electromagnetic induction in generators.

nodes.name: 假设与变量
nodes.subject: science
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 1-5 will be able to formulate a clear, testable hypothesis that predicts a relationship between an independent and a dependent variable.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 1-5 will be able to formulate a clear, testable hypothesis that predicts a relationship between an independent and a dependent variable.
Students will be able to justify their hypothesis by referencing prior scientific knowledge or preliminary observations.

nodes.name: 实验设计
nodes.subject: science
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 2-5 will be able to design a controlled experiment, identifying and justifying the control of variables (independent, dependent, controlled) to ensure a fair test.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 2-5 will be able to design a controlled experiment, identifying and justifying the control of variables (independent, dependent, controlled) to ensure a fair test.
Students will be able to select appropriate equipment and methods, and describe a logical, safe procedure to collect sufficient and relevant data.

nodes.name: 数据分析
nodes.subject: science
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 1-5 will be able to process qualitative and/or quantitative data by constructing appropriate graphs (e.g., bar, line) and calculating means.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 1-5 will be able to process qualitative and/or quantitative data by constructing appropriate graphs (e.g., bar, line) and calculating means.
Students will be able to identify trends and patterns in data, draw conclusions supported by evidence, and evaluate the reliability of their method.

nodes.name: 科学写作
nodes.subject: science
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 1-5 will be able to structure a laboratory report with clear sections (aim, hypothesis, method, results, conclusion, evaluation).
key_concepts: Students in MYP 1-5 will be able to structure a laboratory report with clear sections (aim, hypothesis, method, results, conclusion, evaluation).
Students will be able to communicate findings using scientific language and conventions, including proper units, terminology, and citations where appropriate.

nodes.name: 科学伦理
nodes.subject: science
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to discuss the ethical implications of a scientific development (e.g., genetic engineering, animal testing) by considering different stakeholder perspectives.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to discuss the ethical implications of a scientific development (e.g., genetic engineering, animal testing) by considering different stakeholder perspectives.
Students will be able to explain the importance of honesty, integrity, and peer review in the scientific process, and identify examples of ethical and unethical scientific conduct.

nodes.name: 环境科学
nodes.subject: science
nodes.definition: Students in MYP 2-5 will be able to analyze human impacts (e.g., pollution, deforestation, climate change) on a specific ecosystem and propose scientifically sound mitigation strategies.
key_concepts: Students in MYP 2-5 will be able to analyze human impacts (e.g., pollution, deforestation, climate change) on a specific ecosystem and propose scientifically sound mitigation strategies.
Students will be able to evaluate the sustainability of a resource management practice by considering its environmental, economic, and social impacts.

nodes.name: 口头表达
nodes.subject: inquiry
nodes.definition: Students will be able to use spoken language to share ideas, ask questions, and describe experiences clearly and confidently in small group settings (K-2).
key_concepts: Students will be able to use spoken language to share ideas, ask questions, and describe experiences clearly and confidently in small group settings (K-2).
Students will be able to adapt their oral language for different purposes and audiences, such as giving an informative presentation or participating in a discussion (3-5).

nodes.name: 故事讲述
nodes.subject: inquiry
nodes.definition: Students will be able to identify and sequence the key elements (beginning, middle, end) of a story and retell it using appropriate expression (K-2).
key_concepts: Students will be able to identify and sequence the key elements (beginning, middle, end) of a story and retell it using appropriate expression (K-2).
Students will be able to create and present original narratives, using voice, gesture, and structure to engage an audience and convey meaning (3-5).

nodes.name: 诗歌朗读与创作
nodes.subject: inquiry
nodes.definition: Students will be able to explore and identify simple patterns of sound (e.g., rhyme, rhythm, repetition) in age-appropriate poems (K-2).
key_concepts: Students will be able to explore and identify simple patterns of sound (e.g., rhyme, rhythm, repetition) in age-appropriate poems (K-2).
Students will be able to compose original poetic pieces using figurative language and deliberate structural choices to express personal ideas and emotions (3-5).

nodes.name: 戏剧与角色扮演
nodes.subject: inquiry
nodes.definition: Students will be able to use role-play and simple dramatic conventions (e.g., freeze frames, hot-seating) to explore characters, feelings, and different perspectives (K-2).
key_concepts: Students will be able to use role-play and simple dramatic conventions (e.g., freeze frames, hot-seating) to explore characters, feelings, and different perspectives (K-2).
Students will be able to collaborate to plan, rehearse, and present short devised scenes that communicate a clear message or story (3-5).

nodes.name: 创意写作
nodes.subject: inquiry
nodes.definition: Students will be able to generate, draft, and illustrate simple written texts for enjoyment, using familiar structures and imaginative ideas (K-2).
key_concepts: Students will be able to generate, draft, and illustrate simple written texts for enjoyment, using familiar structures and imaginative ideas (K-2).
Students will be able to apply the writing process (planning, drafting, revising, editing) to produce structured creative texts in various genres (3-5).

nodes.name: 绘画入门
nodes.subject: inquiry
nodes.definition: Students will be able to experiment with a variety of tools and techniques (e.g., line, shape, texture) to represent observations and ideas visually (K-2).
key_concepts: Students will be able to experiment with a variety of tools and techniques (e.g., line, shape, texture) to represent observations and ideas visually (K-2).
Students will be able to use drawing as a tool for inquiry, planning, and detailed visual communication, explaining their artistic choices (3-5).

nodes.name: 色彩理论
nodes.subject: inquiry
nodes.definition: Students will be able to identify primary and secondary colors and explore mixing them to create new hues (K-2).
key_concepts: Students will be able to identify primary and secondary colors and explore mixing them to create new hues (K-2).
Students will be able to investigate and apply color relationships (e.g., warm/cool, complementary) to evoke specific moods or effects in their artwork (3-5).

nodes.name: 绘画与材料
nodes.subject: inquiry
nodes.definition: Students will be able to explore the properties of different paints and application tools to create expressive marks and fill defined areas (K-2).
key_concepts: Students will be able to explore the properties of different paints and application tools to create expressive marks and fill defined areas (K-2).
Students will be able to intentionally select and manipulate painting media and techniques to create artwork that communicates a personal response to a stimulus (3-5).

nodes.name: 雕塑与立体造型
nodes.subject: inquiry
nodes.definition: Students will be able to manipulate and combine a range of materials (e.g., clay, cardboard, found objects) to create simple three-dimensional forms (K-2).
key_concepts: Students will be able to manipulate and combine a range of materials (e.g., clay, cardboard, found objects) to create simple three-dimensional forms (K-2).
Students will be able to design and construct a sculpture, considering elements such as balance, form, and space, to represent an idea or concept (3-5).

nodes.name: 数字艺术
nodes.subject: inquiry
nodes.definition: Students will be able to use basic digital tools (e.g., drawing apps, cameras) to create, capture, and modify simple images (K-2).
key_concepts: Students will be able to use basic digital tools (e.g., drawing apps, cameras) to create, capture, and modify simple images (K-2).
Students will be able to create a digital art piece or composition, demonstrating an understanding of layering, editing, and digital effects to enhance expression (3-5).

nodes.name: 节奏与律动
nodes.subject: inquiry
nodes.definition: Students will be able to identify and replicate simple rhythmic patterns using body percussion, voice, and simple instruments (K-2).
key_concepts: Students will be able to identify and replicate simple rhythmic patterns using body percussion, voice, and simple instruments (K-2).
Students will be able to create and notate (using symbols or standard notation) rhythmic sequences to accompany music or movement pieces (3-5).

nodes.name: 音乐入门
nodes.subject: inquiry
nodes.definition: Students will be able to explore the elements of music (pitch, tempo, dynamics) through listening, singing, and playing tuned/untuned percussion (K-2).
key_concepts: Students will be able to explore the elements of music (pitch, tempo, dynamics) through listening, singing, and playing tuned/untuned percussion (K-2).
Students will be able to compose and perform short melodic phrases, demonstrating an understanding of basic musical structure and notation (3-5).

nodes.name: 舞蹈表达
nodes.subject: inquiry
nodes.definition: Students will be able to explore and combine basic locomotor and non-locomotor movements in response to different stimuli (e.g., music, stories) (K-2).
key_concepts: Students will be able to explore and combine basic locomotor and non-locomotor movements in response to different stimuli (e.g., music, stories) (K-2).
Students will be able to choreograph and perform a short dance sequence that uses space, dynamics, and relationship to express an idea or emotion (3-5).

nodes.name: 戏剧表演
nodes.subject: inquiry
nodes.definition: Students will be able to participate in guided dramatic play and simple performances, understanding the role of an audience (K-2).
key_concepts: Students will be able to participate in guided dramatic play and simple performances, understanding the role of an audience (K-2).
Students will be able to contribute to a collaborative theatre performance, taking on specific responsibilities (e.g., actor, designer, stagehand) and reflecting on the process (3-5).

nodes.name: 节日与庆典
nodes.subject: inquiry
nodes.definition: We invite students, their families and friends to lead these events, whether it is reading stories to students in English or in another language, sharing food or celebrating festivals.
key_concepts: We invite students, their families and friends to lead these events, whether it is reading stories to students in English or in another language, sharing food or celebrating festivals.

nodes.name: 符号与意义
nodes.subject: inquiry
nodes.definition: Students will be able to recognize that symbols, signs, and images communicate meaning and identify examples from their own environment (K-2).
key_concepts: Students will be able to recognize that symbols, signs, and images communicate meaning and identify examples from their own environment (K-2).
Students will be able to analyze how symbols are used in different cultural contexts and art forms to convey messages, beliefs, and values (3-5).

nodes.name: 神话与传说
nodes.subject: inquiry
nodes.definition: Students will be able to listen to and retell myths or legends, identifying central characters and events (K-2).
key_concepts: Students will be able to listen to and retell myths or legends, identifying central characters and events (K-2).
Students will be able to compare myths and legends from different cultures, exploring how they explain natural phenomena, teach lessons, and express cultural identity (3-5).

nodes.name: 家庭角色
nodes.subject: inquiry
nodes.definition: An inquiry into the nature of the self; beliefs and values; personal, physical, mental, social and spiritual health; human relationships including families, friends, communities and cultures; rights and responsibilities; what it means to be human.
key_concepts: An inquiry into the nature of the self; beliefs and values; personal, physical, mental, social and spiritual health; human relationships including families, friends, communities and cultures; rights and responsibilities; what it means to be human.

nodes.name: 学校社区

key_concepts: An inquiry into the nature of the self; beliefs and values; personal, physical, mental, social and spiritual health; human relationships including families, friends, communities and cultures; rights and responsibilities; what it means to be human.

nodes.name: 政府与治理
nodes.subject: inquiry
nodes.definition: Students will be able to identify the basic functions and structures of government (e.g., local, national) and explain how they serve the needs of a community. (Age 9-11)
key_concepts: Students will be able to identify the basic functions and structures of government (e.g., local, national) and explain how they serve the needs of a community. (Age 9-11)
Students will be able to investigate and compare different forms of governance within their own and other societies, using key concepts such as function and responsibility.

nodes.name: 规则与法律

key_concepts: Students will be able to analyze the purpose of rules and laws in different contexts (school, community) and explain the consequences of following or not following them. (Age 7-9)

key_concepts: Students will be able to categorize items as needs or wants and explain how these choices impact personal and community resource allocation. (Age 5-7)
Students will be able to critically examine the influence of culture, advertising, and personal values on perceptions of needs and wants. (Age 9-11)

key_concepts: Students will be able to distinguish between goods (products) and services (actions) and identify examples of each within their local community. (Age 5-7)

key_concepts: Students will be able to explain the role of money as a medium of exchange and investigate simple forms of trade and barter. (Age 7-9)

key_concepts: Students will be able to describe, using simple examples, how the price or availability of a good can be influenced by supply (how much there is) and demand (how many people want it). (Age 7-9)

nodes.name: 工作与职业

nodes.name: 代数表达式

nodes.definition: HSA-SSE.A.1 Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context. a. Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients. b. Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity. For example, interpret P(1+r)^n as the product of P and a factor not depending on P.
key_concepts: HSA-SSE.A.1 Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context. a. Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients. b. Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity. For example, interpret P(1+r)^n as the product of P and a factor not depending on P.

HSA-SSE.A.2 Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it. For example, see x^4 – y^4 as (x^2)^2 – (y^2)^2, thus recognizing it as a difference of squares that can be factored as (x^2 – y^2)(x^2 + y^2).

nodes.name: 一次方程与不等式

HSA-CED.A.4 Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations. For example, rearrange Ohm’s law V = IR to highlight resistance R.

nodes.name: 线性方程组
nodes.subject: math
nodes.definition: HSA-REI.C.5 Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.
key_concepts: HSA-REI.C.5 Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.
HSA-REI.C.6 Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

HSA-REI.C.7 Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically. For example, find the points of intersection between the line y = –3x and the circle x^2 + y^2 = 3.

HSA-REI.D.11 Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

nodes.name: 指数运算

nodes.definition: HSN-RN.A.1 Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents. key_concepts: HSN-RN.A.1 Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents. nodes.name: 因式分解

Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions. For example the expression 1.15^t can be rewritten as (1.15^(1/12))^(12t) ≈ 1.012^(12t) to reveal the approximate equivalent monthly interest rate if the annual rate is 15%.

nodes.name: 一元二次方程

Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x^2 = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

key_concepts: HSF-IF.A.1 Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. Use frequently occurring nouns and verbs. c. Form regular plural nouns orally by adding /s/ or /es/ (e.g., dog, dogs; wish, wishes). d. Understand and use question words (interrogatives) (e.g., who, what, where, when, why, how). e. Use the most frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., to, from, in, out, on, off, for, of, by, with). f. Produce and expand complete sentences in shared language activities.
